collateral_tests|collateral_config|collateral_docs|structural) : ;;
                    *) error "cycle '$cid': scope_policy.auto_grant unknown class '$_cls' (valid: collateral_tests, collateral_config, collateral_docs, structural)"; return 1 ;;
                esac
            done
        fi
        local sesc_var="_TPL_CYCLE_SCOPE_ESCALATE_${safe}"; local sesc="${!sesc_var:-none}"
        case "$sesc" in structural|none) : ;; *) error "cycle '$cid': scope_policy.escalate must be structural|none, got: $sesc"; return 1 ;; esac
        local sod_var="_TPL_CYCLE_SCOPE_ON_DENY_${safe}"; local sod="${!sod_var:-abandon}"
        case "$sod" in abandon) : ;; *) error "cycle '$cid': scope_policy.on_deny must be abandon, got: $sod"; return 1 ;; esac

        # #1284 (ADR-047): multi-condition exit_when replaces the single-condition
        # UNTIL vars. When a combinator is present, validate the N conditions at
        # this preflight layer (mirroring the runtime check in cycle-orchestrator.sh
        # _cycle_load_template); otherwise validate the single-condition until.stage.
        local ew_comb_check_var="_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR_${safe}"
        local ew_comb="${!ew_comb_check_var:-}"
        if [[ -n "$ew_comb" ]]; then
            case "$ew_comb" in
                all|any) : ;;
                *) error "cycle '$cid': exit_when combinator must be all|any, got: $ew_comb"; return 1 ;;
            esac
            local ew_count_var="_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_COUNT_${safe}"
            local ew_count="${!ew_count_var:-}"
            if [[ -z "$ew_count" ]] || ! [[ "$ew_count" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || [[ "$ew_count" -lt 1 ]]; then
                error "cycle '$cid': exit_when multi-condition count must be integer >=1, got: ${ew_count:-<unset>}"
                return 1
            fi
            local ew_i
            for (( ew_i=1; ew_i<=ew_count; ew_i++ )); do
                local _sv="_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_${ew_i}_STAGE_${safe}"
                local _fv="_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_${ew_i}_FIELD_${safe}"
                local _ov="_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_${ew_i}_OP_${safe}"
                local _vv="_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_${ew_i}_VALUE_${safe}"
                local ew_s="${!_sv:-}" ew_f="${!_fv:-}" ew_o="${!_ov:-}" ew_v="${!_vv:-}"
                if [[ -z "$ew_s" || -z "$ew_f" || -z "$ew_o" || -z "$ew_v" ]]; then
                    error "cycle '$cid': exit_when condition $ew_i: {stage,field,op,value} all required"
                    return 1
                fi
                case "$ew_f" in
                    verdict|status) : ;;
                    *) error "cycle '$cid': exit_when condition $ew_i: field must be verdict|status, got: $ew_f"; return 1 ;;
                esac
                case "$ew_o" in
                    eq|ne|in) : ;;
                    *) error "cycle '$cid': exit_when condition $ew_i: op must be eq|ne|in, got: $ew_o"; return 1 ;;
                esac
                local found=0
                for s in "${cs[@]}"; do
                    [[ "$s" == "$ew_s" ]] && found=1 && break
                done
                if [[ $found -ne 1 ]]; then
                    error "cycle '$cid': exit_when condition $ew_i: stage '$ew_s' is not in cycle stages (${cs[*]})"
                    return 1
                fi
            done
        else
            # Single-condition: until.stage must be set and in cs[].
            local us_var="_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_STAGE_${safe}"
            local us="${!us_var:-}"
            if [[ -z "$us" ]]; then
                error "cycle '$cid': until.stage required"
                return 1
            fi
            local found=0
            for s in "${cs[@]}"; do
                [[ "$s" == "$us" ]] && found=1 && break
            done
            if [[ $found -ne 1 ]]; then
                error "cycle '$cid': until.stage '$us' is not in cycle stages (${cs[*]})"
                return 1
            fi
        fi
    done
    return 0
}

# ─── _tpl_validate_parallel — enforce ADR-039 invariants ─────────────────────
# - each group has >=1 member
# - members disjoint from cycle members and from other parallel groups
# - max_parallel is empty or a positive integer
# - on_member_error ∈ {continue, collect}
_tpl_validate_parallel() {
    [[ ${#_TPL_PARALLEL_GROUPS[@]} -eq 0 ]] && return 0

    # Build the set of all cycle members for disjointness checks.
    local -A cycle_member=()
    local cid
    for cid in "${_TPL_CYCLES[@]}"; do
        local c_safe="${cid//-/_}"
        local c_var="_TPL_CYCLE_STAGES_${c_safe}"
        local c_csv="${!c_var:-}"
        local c_IFS_save="$IFS"; IFS=','
        # shellcheck disable=SC2206
        local -a cms=($c_csv)
        IFS="$c_IFS_save"
        local cm
        for cm in "${cms[@]}"; do
            [[ -n "$cm" ]] && cycle_member[$cm]=1
        done
    done

    local gid
    local -A seen_member=()
    for gid in "${_TPL_PARALLEL_GROUPS[@]}"; do
        local safe="${gid//-/_}"
        local flow_var="_TPL_PARALLEL_FLOW_${safe}"
        local flow_csv="${!flow_var:-}"
        local g_IFS_save="$IFS"; IFS=','
        # shellcheck disable=SC2206
        local -a ms=($flow_csv)
        IFS="$g_IFS_save"

        # >=1 member
        local member_count=0 m
        for m in "${ms[@]}"; do
            [[ -n "$m" ]] && member_count=$((member_count + 1))
        done
        if [[ $member_count -eq 0 ]]; then
            error "parallel group '$gid': no members declared (>=1 required)"
            return 1
        fi

        for m in "${ms[@]}"; do
            [[ -z "$m" ]] && continue
            if [[ -n "${cycle_member[$m]:-}" ]]; then
                error "parallel group '$gid': member '$m' is also a cycle member (parallel members must be disjoint from cycles)"
                return 1
            fi
            if [[ -n "${seen_member[$m]:-}" ]]; then
                error "parallel group '$gid': member '$m' is in another parallel group (parallel groups must not overlap)"
                return 1
            fi
            seen_member[$m]=1
        done

        # max_parallel: empty (unbounded) or a positive integer.
        local max_var="_TPL_PARALLEL_MAX_${safe}"
        local max="${!max_var:-}"
        if [[ -n "$max" ]]; then
            if ! [[ "$max" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || [[ "$max" -lt 1 ]]; then
                error "parallel group '$gid': max_parallel must be empty or a positive integer, got: $max"
                return 1
            fi
        fi

        # on_member_error: closed vocabulary (the template names behavior).
        local onerr_var="_TPL_PARALLEL_ON_ERR_${safe}"
        local onerr="${!onerr_var:-continue}"
        case "$onerr" in
            continue|collect) : ;;
            *) error "parallel group '$gid': on_member_error must be continue|collect, got: $onerr"; return 1 ;;
        esac
    done
    return 0
}

# ─── _tpl_build_dispatch_units — assemble runner dispatch sequence ───────────
# Walks _TPL_STAGES[] in order. Each stage belongs to at most one cycle
# (validated above). On entering a cycle's first stage, emit one "cycle:<id>"
# unit covering the whole cycle. All other stages become "stage:<id>".
#
# ADR-026 / Wave 18-B (#707): when cycles nest (a cycle's `flow:` member is
# itself a cycle), the OUTERMOST enclosing cycle owns dispatch — the runner
# invokes cycle_orchestrator_run on the outermost, which then recurses into
# inner cycles via _TPL_STAGE_TYPE_<id>=cycle (Wave 17-B). The dispatch
# sequence must emit exactly one `cycle:<outermost>` unit covering all leaf
# stages reachable from the outermost cycle, in their _TPL_STAGES order.
# Without this folding, a leaf member of an inner cycle that is also the
# first member of the outer cycle would be absorbed into `cycle:<inner>`
# and the OUTER cycle would never appear in dispatch, silently dropping
# the outer-cycle semantics (exit_when, abort_when, feedback).
_tpl_build_dispatch_units() {
    _TPL_DISPATCH_UNITS=()
    # Map: stage → immediate enclosing cycle id (if any)
    local -A stage_to_cycle=()
    # Map: cycle_id → its parent cycle id (if any). A cycle A is the parent
    # of cycle B when A's CSV-stage list contains B as a member.
    local -A cycle_parent=()
    # Build a quick "is this id a registered cycle" set. We CANNOT rely on
    # _TPL_STAGE_TYPE_<id> here because _tpl_build_dispatch_units runs in
    # load_template BEFORE the type discriminator vars are populated. The
    # _TPL_CYCLES array IS populated by this point (translator topo pre-pass
    # registers cycles before this function fires).
    local -A is_cycle=()
    local _c
    for _c in "${_TPL_CYCLES[@]}"; do is_cycle[$_c]=1; done
    # ADR-039 (#1132): set of registered parallel group ids — a cycle's flow
    # member may name one; its LEAF members must fold under the enclosing
    # cycle unit (not a separate top-level "parallel:<gid>").
    local -A is_parallel=()
    local _pgid
    for _pgid in "${_TPL_PARALLEL_GROUPS[@]}"; do is_parallel[$_pgid]=1; done

    local cid
    for cid in "${_TPL_CYCLES[@]}"; do
        local safe="${cid//-/_}"
        local stages_var="_TPL_CYCLE_STAGES_${safe}"
        local stages_csv="${!stages_var:-}"
        local IFS_save="$IFS"; IFS=','
        # shellcheck disable=SC2206
        local -a cs=($stages_csv)
        IFS="$IFS_save"
        local s
        for s in "${cs[@]}"; do
            if [[ -n "${is_cycle[$s]:-}" ]]; then
                cycle_parent[$s]="$cid"
            elif [[ -n "${is_parallel[$s]:-}" ]]; then
                # ADR-039 (#1132): map the group's leaf members to the enclosing
                # cycle so they absorb under "cycle:<id>". Without this the leaves
                # would map only to stage_to_parallel and emit a stray top-level
                # "parallel:<gid>" unit, double-dispatching the group.
                local _pg_safe="${s//-/_}"
                local _pg_flow_var="_TPL_PARALLEL_FLOW_${_pg_safe}"
                local _pg_csv="${!_pg_flow_var:-}"
                local _pg_ifs="$IFS"; IFS=','
                # shellcheck disable=SC2206
                local -a _pg_ms=($_pg_csv)
                IFS="$_pg_ifs"
                local _pgm
                for _pgm in "${_pg_ms[@]}"; do
                    [[ -z "$_pgm" ]] && continue
                    [[ -z "${stage_to_cycle[$_pgm]:-}" ]] && stage_to_cycle[$_pgm]="$cid"
                done
            else
                # Inner cycle's claim wins over outer when they overlap (which
                # shouldn't happen under acyclicity, but be explicit). Don't
                # overwrite an existing entry.
                [[ -z "${stage_to_cycle[$s]:-}" ]] && stage_to_cycle[$s]="$cid"
            fi
        done
    done

    # Resolve each cycle to its outermost ancestor.
    local -A cycle_outermost=()
    for cid in "${_TPL_CYCLES[@]}"; do
        local cur="$cid" parent
        while :; do
            parent="${cycle_parent[$cur]:-}"
            [[ -z "$parent" ]] && break
            cur="$parent"
        done
        cycle_outermost[$cid]="$cur"
    done

    # ADR-039 (#1130): map each leaf stage → its enclosing parallel group (if
    # any). A parallel group folds to one "parallel:<gid>" unit, symmetric to
    # "cycle:<id>". Validation guarantees members are disjoint from cycles, so a
    # stage is in at most one of {cycle, parallel}.
    local -A stage_to_parallel=()
    local pg
    for pg in "${_TPL_PARALLEL_GROUPS[@]}"; do
        local psafe="${pg//-/_}"
        local pflow_var="_TPL_PARALLEL_FLOW_${psafe}"
        local pflow_csv="${!pflow_var:-}"
        local p_IFS_save="$IFS"; IFS=','
        # shellcheck disable=SC2206
        local -a pms=($pflow_csv)
        IFS="$p_IFS_save"
        local pm
        for pm in "${pms[@]}"; do
            [[ -z "$pm" ]] && continue
            [[ -z "${stage_to_parallel[$pm]:-}" ]] && stage_to_parallel[$pm]="$pg"
        done
    done

    # issue #1295 (ADR-047 §2): build a set of map group ids for O(1) lookup.
    # Map groups appear IN _TPL_STAGES (as the group id itself, not as members)
    # and emit a "map:<gid>" dispatch unit rather than "stage:<gid>".
    local -A is_map_group=()
    local _mg
    for _mg in "${_TPL_MAP_GROUPS[@]}"; do is_map_group[$_mg]=1; done

    local s
    local -A emitted_outer=()
    local -A emitted_parallel=()
    for s in "${_TPL_STAGES[@]}"; do
        local in_cycle="${stage_to_cycle[$s]:-}"
        local in_parallel="${stage_to_parallel[$s]:-}"
        if [[ -n "$in_cycle" ]]; then
            local outer="${cycle_outermost[$in_cycle]:-$in_cycle}"
            if [[ -z "${emitted_outer[$outer]:-}" ]]; then
                _TPL_DISPATCH_UNITS+=("cycle:$outer")
                emitted_outer[$outer]=1
            fi
            # subsequent stages absorbed under the outermost cycle unit
        elif [[ -n "$in_parallel" ]]; then
            if [[ -z "${emitted_parallel[$in_parallel]:-}" ]]; then
                _TPL_DISPATCH_UNITS+=("parallel:$in_parallel")
                emitted_parallel[$in_parallel]=1
            fi
            # subsequent members absorbed under the same parallel unit
        elif [[ -n "${is_map_group[$s]:-}" ]]; then
            # issue #1295: map group id is itself in _TPL_STAGES; emit one map unit.
            _TPL_DISPATCH_UNITS+=("map:$s")
        else
            _TPL_DISPATCH_UNITS+=("stage:$s")
        fi
    done
    return 0
}

# ADR-015 v3 (#440): validate tail_lines (integer 1..10000) and redact (true|false)
# ADR-017 (#455): also validate router.timeout_s (integer 1..3600)
# ADR-018 (#466): also validate router.max_turns (integer 1..200)
# ADR-018 (#467): also validate router.max_iterations (integer 1..50)
# ADR-029 (#1230): also validate router.retries (integer 0..10; 0 = opt-out).
# Uses Bash 5+ namerefs for safer array-by-name passing (no eval indirection).
_tpl_validate_io_knobs() {
    local -n ids_ref="$1"
    local -n tails_ref="$2"
    local -n redacts_ref="$3"
    local -n rtimeouts_ref="$4"
    local -n rmaxturns_ref="$5"
    local -n rmaxiters_ref="$6"
    local -n rretries_ref="$7"
    local i n=${#ids_ref[@]}
    for (( i=0; i<n; i++ )); do
        local stage="${ids_ref[$i]}"
        local tail="${tails_ref[$i]}"
        local redact="${redacts_ref[$i]}"
        local rt="${rtimeouts_ref[$i]}"
        local rmt="${rmaxturns_ref[$i]}"
        local rmi="${rmaxiters_ref[$i]}"
        local rre="${rretries_ref[$i]}"
        if [[ -n "$tail" ]]; then
            if ! [[ "$tail" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || [[ "$tail" -lt 1 ]] || [[ "$tail" -gt 10000 ]]; then
                error "template: io.tail_lines for stage '$stage' must be integer in 1..10000, got: $tail"
                return 1
            fi
        fi
        if [[ -n "$redact" ]]; then
            if [[ "$redact" != "true" && "$redact" != "false" ]]; then
                error "template: io.redact for stage '$stage' must be 'true' or 'false', got: $redact"
                return 1
            fi
        fi
        if [[ -n "$rt" ]]; then
            if ! [[ "$rt" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || [[ "$rt" -lt 1 ]] || [[ "$rt" -gt 3600 ]]; then
                error "template: router.timeout_s for stage '$stage' must be integer in 1..3600, got: $rt"
                return 1
            fi
        fi
        if [[ -n "$rmt" ]]; then
            # ADR-018 Amendment N (#762): max_turns=0 is a sentinel meaning
            # "omit --max-turns flag from claude argv". Negatives and >200
            # remain invalid.
            if ! [[ "$rmt" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || [[ "$rmt" -gt 200 ]]; then
                error "template: router.max_turns for stage '$stage' must be integer in 0..200, got: $rmt"
                return 1
            fi
        fi
        if [[ -n "$rmi" ]]; then
            if ! [[ "$rmi" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || [[ "$rmi" -lt 1 ]] || [[ "$rmi" -gt 50 ]]; then
                error "template: router.max_iterations for stage '$stage' must be integer in 1..50, got: $rmi"
                return 1
            fi
        fi
        if [[ -n "$rre" ]]; then
            # ADR-029 (#1230): retries=0 is the explicit opt-out and valid.
            if ! [[ "$rre" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || [[ "$rre" -gt 10 ]]; then
                error "template: router.retries for stage '$stage' must be integer in 0..10, got: $rre"
                return 1
            fi
        fi
    done
    return 0
}

# _tpl_validate_io_dests <ids_arr_name> <dests_arr_name>
# Validates io.destinations tokens (v1 set: file, stdout, gh_comment).
# Bash 3.2 compat: pass array names; iterate via eval-style indirection.
_tpl_validate_io_dests() {
    local ids_var="$1" dests_var="$2"
    local valid_list="${_ZBUILD_IO_DESTINATIONS_VALID[*]}"
    # shellcheck disable=SC1087,SC2154
    # _n / _stage / _dests are assigned via the eval lines below; shellcheck
    # can't see through eval so it warns SC2154 ("referenced but not assigned").
    # Pre-declare them as locals so the disable comments don't need to repeat.
    local _n="" _stage="" _dests=""
    eval "_n=\${#${ids_var}[@]}"
    local i
    for (( i=0; i<_n; i++ )); do
        eval "_stage=\${${ids_var}[$i]}"
        eval "_dests=\${${dests_var}[$i]}"
        [[ -z "$_dests" ]] && continue
        local token
        local IFS_save="$IFS"
        IFS=','
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        set -- $_dests
        IFS="$IFS_save"
        for token in "$@"; do
            [[ -z "$token" ]] && continue
            local found=0
            local v
            for v in "${_ZBUILD_IO_DESTINATIONS_VALID[@]}"; do
                [[ "$v" == "$token" ]] && { found=1; break; }
            done
            if [[ $found -eq 0 ]]; then
                error "template: unknown io.destination '$token' for stage '$_stage' (valid: $valid_list)"
                return 1
            fi
        done
    done
    return 0
}

# ─── ADR-027 helpers (Wave 17-B #703) ─────────────────────────────────────────
#
# ─── _tpl_parse_always_run <file> (#1831) ────────────────────────────────────
# Emit one `<id>|<roles>|<timeout_s>` line per entry in the template's top-level
# `always_run:` list, in declared order.
#
# SHAPE-INDEPENDENT on purpose. `always_run:` is a top-level key and its members
# are top-level sections in BOTH the ADR-027 shape and the legacy one, so this
# reads the file directly rather than riding either shape's row stream. The
# first cut of #1831 parsed it inside the new-shape translator; every old-shape
# template then silently lost its always-run stages, and the parity fixture
# (old shape, `extends: simple`) stopped running teardown at all.
#
# `roles` is emitted as the sentinel `__MISSING__` when the named stage has no
# top-level section, so the caller can tell "declared but undefined" (refuse the
# template) from "defined but roles-less" (also refuse, different message).
# Order is preserved by walking the list, not the section map.
_tpl_parse_always_run() {
    local file="$1"
    [[ -f "$file" ]] || return 0
    awk '
        function trim(x) { gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", x); return x }
        # Top-level always_run:, block form.
        /^always_run:[[:space:]]*$/ { in_ar = 1; in_sec = ""; next }
        # Inline form: always_run: [a, b]
        /^always_run:[[:space:]]*\[/ {
            line = $0
            sub(/^[^[]*\[/, "", line); sub(/\].*$/, "", line)
            gsub(/[[:space:]]/, "", line)
            n = split(line, items, /,/)
            for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) if (items[i] != "") { ar_n++; ar[ar_n] = items[i] }
            in_ar = 0; in_sec = ""; next
        }
        in_ar && /^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]/ {
            item = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]+/, "", item); item = trim(item)
            if (item != "") { ar_n++; ar[ar_n] = item }
            next
        }
        # Any other top-level key closes the list and opens a possible section.
        /^[a-zA-Z_]/ {
            in_ar = 0; in_router = 0; in_roles = 0
            in_sec = $0; sub(/:.*$/, "", in_sec); in_sec = trim(in_sec)
            seen[in_sec] = 1
            next
        }
        # Within a section: roles: and router.timeout_s.
        # BOTH list forms, because `_tpl_parse_stages_v2` accepts both and a
        # template author will model an always-run section on a flow stage.
        # Accepting only the inline form here would refuse a section that looks
        # exactly like every other one in the file.
        in_sec != "" && /^[[:space:]]+roles:/ {
            v = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+roles:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); v = trim(v)
            if (v ~ /\[/) {
                gsub(/^\[|\]$/, "", v); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, "", v)
                roles[in_sec] = v
                in_roles = 0
            } else if (v == "") {
                # Block form: the items are the indented `- x` lines below.
                in_roles = 1; roles[in_sec] = ""
            } else {
                roles[in_sec] = v
                in_roles = 0
            }
            in_router = 0
            next
        }
        in_sec != "" && in_roles && /^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]/ {
            v = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]+/, "", v); v = trim(v)
            if (v != "") roles[in_sec] = (roles[in_sec] == "" ? v : roles[in_sec] "," v)
            next
        }
        in_sec != "" && /^[[:space:]]+router:[[:space:]]*$/ { in_router = 1; in_roles = 0; next }
        in_sec != "" && in_router && /^[[:space:]]+timeout_s:/ {
            v = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+timeout_s:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); to[in_sec] = trim(v)
            next
        }
        # A key at section-attribute depth that is not router: closes the router block.
        in_sec != "" && /^[[:space:]]+[a-zA-Z_]+:/ && !/^[[:space:]]+timeout_s:/ { in_router = 0; in_roles = 0 }
        END {
            for (i = 1; i <= ar_n; i++) {
                id = ar[i]
                if (!(id in seen)) { printf "%s|__MISSING__|\n", id; continue }
                printf "%s|%s|%s\n", id, (id in roles ? roles[id] : ""), (id in to ? to[id] : "")
            }
        }
    ' "$file"
}

# _tpl_is_new_shape — heuristic: top-level `flow:` key AND NO top-level
# `stages:` key indicates ADR-027 shape. The two never coexist; if both
# appear we treat as old shape (safer default — old-shape parser is mature).
_tpl_is_new_shape() {
    local file="$1"
    local has_flow=0 has_stages=0
    # Copilot P2: accept both block form `flow:\n  - x` AND inline list form
    # `flow: [a, b]`. Either matches.
    if awk 'BEGIN{rc=1} /^flow:[[:space:]]*$/ {rc=0; exit} /^flow:[[:space:]]*\[/ {rc=0; exit} END{exit rc}' "$file"; then
        has_flow=1
    fi
    if awk 'BEGIN{rc=1} /^stages:[[:space:]]*$/ {rc=0; exit} END{exit rc}' "$file"; then
        has_stages=1
    fi
    [[ $has_flow -eq 1 && $has_stages -eq 0 ]]
}

# _tpl_translate_new_shape — read an ADR-027 template and emit the same
# pipe-delimited row stream that _tpl_parse_stages_v2 + _tpl_parse_stage_definitions
# emit for the old shape. Output is two streams separated by an ASCII Unit
# Separator (\037): <stage_rows>\037<defs_rows>.
#
# Strategy: a single AWK pass walks the file in two phases:
#   1. Read top-level `flow:` block → ordered list of stage IDs.
#   2. Read every top-level stage section (key at column 0, not in the
#      reserved set {id, name, extends, defaults, flow, _comment}). For each
#      section emit either:
#        - a defs-style row (always — gives downstream the attr payload), AND
#        - a stage row in flow-order:
#            * leaf  → S| row in the position determined by the top-level
#                      flow index
#            * cycle → IC| row at that position + FB| rows for feedback
# Keeping the existing pipe schema means downstream consumers (validators,
# orchestrator, runner) need zero changes.
_tpl_translate_new_shape() {
    local file="$1"
    awk -v US=$'\037' '
    function trim(s) { sub(/^[[:space:]]+/, "", s); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", s); return s }
    function strip_inline_list(line,    s) {
        s = line; sub(/^[^[]*\[/, "", s); sub(/\].*$/, "", s)
        gsub(/[[:space:]]/, "", s); return s
    }
    function is_reserved(k) {
        # Template-level metadata keys (not stage sections). merge_policy is an
        # ADR-037 §4 per-template knob; reserving it stops the new-shape
        # translator from emitting it as a phantom stage definition (#968 review).
        return (k == "id" || k == "name" || k == "extends" || k == "defaults" \
                || k == "flow" || k == "_comment" || k == "merge_policy" \
                || k == "always_run")
    }

145	# Globals (not local) so EXIT trap can read them after main() returns.
146	_runner_run_id="" _runner_issue="" _runner_ended=false _runner_state_file=""
147	# #1878: last reported snapshot-failure reason, so a static precondition is
148	# reported once rather than once per stage boundary.

151	# ─── _runner_retry_budget <stage> (#2187, was #1887's redispatch budget) ─────
152	# How many times a stage whose disposition says `retry` is re-dispatched. The
153	# word never carries a count: the template's per-stage `retry:` wins, then the
154	# ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_REDISPATCH knob, then the engine default 3. Capped at 5 —
155	# the cycle re-runs its members anyway, so this is not a budget for grinding.
156	# A value above the cap clamps to the cap; a non-number is ignored.
157	_runner_retry_budget() {
158	    local v=""
159	    if declare -F template_stage_retry >/dev/null 2>&1; then
160	        v="$(template_stage_retry "${1:-}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
161	    fi
162	    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || v="${ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_REDISPATCH:-}"
163	    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || v=3
164	    (( v > 5 )) && v=5

168	# ─── _runner_leaf_contract_halt <state_file> <stage> <reason> ───────────────
169	# A leaf stage whose v2 result the engine rejected ends the run; rc 0 when it
170	# did. A cycle already halts on this (#550); a leaf recorded `error` and went on,
171	# which is how #1835's run shipped a plan result with no `reason`. Safe ahead of
172	# #1798: a contract violation is a zBuild defect (ADR-054 §6 `broken`), never a
173	# transient failure, so this cannot turn a network hiccup into a dead run.
174	# Reads main()'s _runner_run_id / _runner_issue and sets its _runner_ended.
175	_runner_leaf_contract_halt() {
176	    local sf="$1" st="$2" why="${3:-}"
177	    [[ "$why" == contract_violation:* ]] || return 1
178	    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
179	    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
180	    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" 2>/dev/null || true
181	    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" \
182	        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
183	    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
184	    _runner_ended=true
185	    error "Stage $st wrote a result the engine rejects ($why) — a zBuild defect; the run stops here"
186	    return 0

189	# ─── _runner_leaf_verdict_halt <state_file> <stage> <class> <raw> ────────────
190	# #1798 (ADR-054 §4): a leaf stage that reports a failure ends the run; rc 0
191	# when it did. <class> is the classified verdict the runner already read
192	# (runner_read_stage_verdict: fail, or a structural word passed through);
193	# <raw> is the stage's own word, which the run's end names. A cycle acts on its
194	# members' verdicts; a leaf used to record one, pick a glyph from it and
195	# complete anyway. A template opts a stage out with `blocking: false`
196	# (ADR-013) — advisory by declaration, never by accident.
197	_runner_leaf_verdict_halt() {
198	    local sf="$1" st="$2" v="${3:-}" raw="${4:-}"
199	    case "$v" in
200	        fail|error|block|scope_violation|corrupt_diff) ;;
201	        *) return 1 ;;
202	    esac
203	    [[ "$(template_stage_blocking "$st" 2>/dev/null)" == "false" ]] && return 1
204	    [[ -n "$raw" && "$raw" != "missing" ]] || raw="$v"
205	    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
206	    _zbuild_state_set_stage_verdict "$sf" "$st" "$v"
207	    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
208	    # No `rc=` field: the stage exited 0, so a verdict-triggered stage.fail
209	    # carries the stage's word (`verdict=`) instead — as the contract halt
210	    # carries `reason=` alone. A consumer of stage.fail reads either shape.
211	    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "verdict=$raw" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" 2>/dev/null || true
212	    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" \
213	        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
214	    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
215	    _runner_ended=true
216	    error "Stage $st reported $raw — the run stops here"
217	    return 0
218	}

220	# ─── _runner_attempt_made_progress <artifact_dir> <stage> <iter> (#2187) ─────
221	# Attempts are numbered from 1 (attempt-archive.sh writes n+1).
222	# rc 0 when the stage's LATEST attempt in this iteration changed any of its
223	# declared outputs (the #2186 attempt record), or when there is no record to
224	# judge by; rc 1 when every output it recorded came back unchanged or absent —
225	# retrying the same work would hit the same wall.
226	_runner_attempt_made_progress() {
227	    local base="${1:-}/attempts/${2//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}" iter="${3:-0}"
228	    [[ -d "$base" ]] || return 0
229	    local latest="" n=0 d k
230	    for d in "$base"/iter-"$iter"-attempt-*; do
231	        [[ -f "$d/attempt.json" ]] || continue
232	        k="${d##*-attempt-}"
233	        [[ "$k" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
234	        (( k > n )) && { n="$k"; latest="$d/attempt.json"; }
235	    done
236	    [[ -n "$latest" ]] || return 0
237	    # #2252: the archive's own judgement of the WORK, when it made one.
238	    if jq -e 'has("progress")' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
239	        jq -e '.progress == true' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1
240	        return
241	    fi
242	    jq -e 'has("outputs") | not' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
243	    jq -e '[.outputs[]] | any(. == "changed")' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1
244	}

246	# ─── _runner_note_push_failure <stage> (#2187) ───────────────────────────────
247	# Report a failed stage-end push once per distinct reason, on the same channel
248	# and dedupe as a failed snapshot.
249	_runner_note_push_failure() {
250	    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "failed" ]] || return 0
251	    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]] || return 0
252	    _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
253	    eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" "stage=${1:-unknown}" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
254	        "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
255	    warn "stage-end push failed at stage '${1:-unknown}': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
256	}

258	# ─── _runner_push_work_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2187) ────────────────────
259	# When the run has a work branch on origin (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH — CI sets
260	# zbuild/issue-N-ci), push the run's commits to it at every stage end, so a new
261	# session can pick them up even if this runner dies. Only when HEAD carries
262	# commits past the intake baseline. Advisory: a failure is reported, never fatal.
263	_runner_push_work_branch() {
264	    local _branch="${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}"
265	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
266	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
267	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
268	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
269	    git -C "$_repo" remote get-url origin >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
270	    local _base=""
271	    [[ -f "${1:-}/intake-baseline-ref.txt" ]] && _base="$(cat "${1:-}/intake-baseline-ref.txt" 2>/dev/null || true)"
272	    if [[ -n "$_base" ]]; then
273	        local _ahead; _ahead="$(git -C "$_repo" rev-list --count "$_base..HEAD" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
274	        [[ "$_ahead" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_ahead" -gt 0 ]] || return 0
275	    fi
276	    local _err
277	    if _err="$(git -C "$_repo" push --force -q origin "HEAD:refs/heads/$_branch" 2>&1)"; then
278	        return 0
279	    fi
280	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
281	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="git push work branch $_branch failed: $(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_err" | cut -c1-300)"
282	    _runner_note_push_failure "${2:-unknown}"
283	    return 0
284	}

286	# ─── _runner_keep_head_on_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2264) ─────────────────
287	# A model call can leave HEAD off the run branch; every later commit then lands
288	# on HEAD alone while the branch ref — which pr-open checks out and the post-run
289	# step pushes — falls behind. #1844 run 37066147994 lost its work that way. At
290	# every stage end, put HEAD back on the branch when that drops nothing, and say
291	# which stage left it off; when the two diverged, move nothing and say so.
292	_runner_keep_head_on_branch() {
293	    local _sd="${1:-}" _stage="${2:-unknown}" _branch=""
294	    [[ -f "$_sd/intake-branch.txt" ]] && read -r _branch 2>/dev/null < "$_sd/intake-branch.txt"
295	    _branch="${_branch//[[:space:]]/}"
296	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
297	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
298	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
299	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
300	    zbuild_keep_head_on_branch "$_repo" "$_branch"
301	    case "$ZBUILD_HEAD_OUTCOME" in
302	        reattached)
303	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.reattached" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
304	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
305	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch ($ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS) — moved '$_branch' to HEAD" ;;
306	        diverged)
307	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.diverged" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
308	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
309	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch and the two diverged — '$_branch' not moved" ;;
310	    esac
311	    return 0
312	}

314	# ─── _runner_snapshot_artifacts <state_dir> <stage> (ADR-050, #1581/#1878) ───
315	# Snapshot the artifact area onto the state branch at a stage boundary, so a
316	# completed stage's work survives a mid-run crash/rate-limit and is available to
317	# the next run. Stage-agnostic (snapshots whatever files exist) and advisory —
318	# never blocks a run.
319	#
320	# #1878: ONE definition, called from every stage-completion site on the LIVE
321	# dispatch-unit path. It previously existed only inline in the legacy linear stage
322	# loop below — which no shipped template ever reaches (any cycle/map/parallel unit
323	# sets _run_dispatch_units=1, and every terminal branch of that block returns), so
324	# the snapshot was never invoked at all and the store was always empty. That is
325	# item 1 of #1807.
326	#
327	# #1878: also no longer swallows stderr. A snapshot that fails now says so, with
328	# the failing git operation named, instead of returning 1 into a `2>/dev/null`
329	# and leaving no trace anywhere.
330	_runner_snapshot_artifacts() {
331	    # $1 may be empty: the cycle-orchestrator call site is several frames from
332	    # main(), and relying on main()'s `state_dir` local reaching it through
333	    # dynamic scope is exactly the kind of implicit coupling that makes a call
334	    # site silently no-op. The runner exports the resolved per-run value at
335	    # runner.sh:1739, so fall back to that.
336	    local _snap_state_dir="${1:-}" _snap_stage="${2:-unknown}"
337	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || _snap_state_dir="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
338	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || return 0
339	    # Before the identity guard: a --goal or local run needs its branch kept too.
340	    _runner_keep_head_on_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
341	    # #1931: identity, not issue number. `issue > 0` excluded every --goal run
342	    # from the durable store, so nothing was ever snapshotted for one and the
343	    # push had nothing to send.
344	    _artifact_persist_has_identity "$_runner_issue" || return 0
345	
346	    _artifact_persist_snapshot "$_snap_state_dir" "$_runner_issue" || true
347	    case "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" in
348	        saved)
349	            eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.saved" \
350	                "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
351	                "skipped=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SKIPPED:-0}" 2>/dev/null || true
352	            ;;
353	        failed)
354	            # Loud, not fatal. This event is the whole point of #1878: the defect
355	            # went undiagnosed for the life of the feature because the failure had
356	            # no channel to surface on.
357	            #
358	            # Deduped on the reason. Most failures are a STATIC precondition — no
359	            # resolvable repository, a ref D/F conflict — so they recur identically
360	            # at every stage boundary. Reporting the first occurrence keeps the
361	            # signal; repeating it once per stage is noise that trains an operator
362	            # to ignore the event. A CHANGED reason is always reported.
363	            if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]]; then
364	                _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
365	                eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" \
366	                    "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
367	                    "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
368	                warn "artifact snapshot failed at stage '$_snap_stage': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
369	            fi
370	            ;;
371	        # empty / unchanged are not failures and are not events: emitting
372	        # `saved` for them is precisely the lie this change removes.
373	        *) : ;;
374	    esac
375	    # #2187: push at the stage end, not only when the run ends — a run killed
376	    # mid-way (job ceiling, SIGKILL) otherwise loses everything since its start.
377	    # Only for a run that declares where its work goes (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH;
378	    # the CI pipeline sets it). A plain local run — and every test — pushes
379	    # nothing here: tests have left state branches in real checkouts, and
380	    # this would put them on origin. The persist stage still pushes at the end.
381	    [[ -n "${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}" ]] || return 0
382	    local _leak=""
383	    if _leak="$(_artifact_persist_find_secret "$_snap_state_dir/artifacts")"; then
384	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
385	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="refusing to push — artifact looks like it carries a credential (${_leak})"
386	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
387	        # The scan covers the artifact area, not the working tree: the run's
388	        # code commits still go to the work branch.
389	        _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
390	        return 0
391	    fi
392	    if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "saved" ]]; then
393	        _artifact_persist_push "$_runner_issue" "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}" || true
394	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
395	    fi
396	    _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
397	    return 0
398	}

401	# Populated immediately before _render_stage_divider for each stage; read at
402	# the ✓/✗ complete/fail sites to compute the duration suffix. assoc array so
403	# nested / out-of-order stages (none today, but safe) still resolve correctly.
404	declare -gA _RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS=()

406	# ─── pipeline-wide start time cache (#525) ───────────────────────────────────
407	# Populated once at the top of main() right after _runner_run_id is sanitized
408	# (well before the EXIT trap installs) so every pipeline.end emit site — incl.
409	# preflight failure (L289) and the EXIT trap — can render a duration. Empty

413	# ─── _runner_now_ms (#508) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
414	# Millisecond wall clock. Honors ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE so goldens
415	# can pin the timestamp (same env var as stage-io.sh — single test contract;
416	# do NOT introduce a runner-specific override name). Non-numeric override is
417	# treated as unset (defensive: a stray export shouldn't crash the runner).
418	# Empty stdout on failure → caller renders "??:??:?? UTC" / "?s" — no crash.
419	_runner_now_ms() {
420	    local ovr="${ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE:-}"
421	    if [[ -n "$ovr" && "$ovr" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
422	        printf '%s' "$ovr"

424	    fi
425	    if [[ -n "${EPOCHREALTIME:-}" ]]; then
426	        local us="${EPOCHREALTIME/./}"
427	        printf '%s' $(( 10#${us} / 1000 ))
428	        return 0
429	    fi
430	    printf '%s' "$(( ${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date -u +%s)} * 1000 ))"

433	# ─── _runner_status_comment_spawn <state_dir> <events_jsonl> <repo_root> ─────
434	# #2131 (ADR-064): the live run-status comment is a SIDECAR that tails
435	# events.jsonl — the engine never renders GitHub markdown itself, it only
436	# starts an observer and stops it. Spawned here, in the runner, so a local
437	# `zbuild pipeline start --issue N` and the CI workflow share one code path
438	# (CI needs no extra step: GITHUB_TOKEN is already job-level env). Every
439	# gate that keeps a test's temp repo off GitHub lives in rsc_enabled; the
440	# harness also pins ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT=0. The sidecar's fd 3 is closed so
441	# it never holds the stage-io channel open.
442	_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
443	_runner_status_comment_spawn() {
444	    local state_dir="$1" events_jsonl="$2" repo_root="${3:-$PWD}"
445	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
446	    # The explicit kill switch leaves NO trace — not even a log line. The
447	    # parity golden lists every file in the state dir, and every test runs
448	    # with the switch on (run-tests.sh); a "disabled" file there would be
449	    # noise in every fixture for a fact the operator already knows.
450	    [[ "${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT:-1}" == "0" ]] && return 0
451	    local lib="$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh"
452	    [[ -f "$lib" ]] || return 0
453	    # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh
454	    source "$lib" 2>/dev/null || return 0
455	    rsc_enabled "$state_dir" "$repo_root" || return 0
456	    local slug; slug="$(zbuild_repo_slug "$repo_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
457	    ( exec 3>&- 2>/dev/null
458	      exec bash "$lib" --events "$events_jsonl" --state-dir "$state_dir" \
459	           --parent-pid $$ --slug "$slug" --issue "${ZBUILD_ISSUE:-0}" \
460	           --run-id "${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-}" --repo-root "$repo_root" ) \
461	        </dev/null >>"$state_dir/status-comment.log" 2>&1 &
462	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=$!
463	    return 0
464	}

466	# ─── _runner_status_comment_reap ─────────────────────────────────────────────
467	# Idempotent (clears the pid first) and rc-neutral (`return 0`, every line
468	# tolerant): it runs inside the EXIT trap under `set -e`, and the process exit
469	# status must never depend on GitHub. TERM, bounded wait, KILL backstop.
470	_runner_status_comment_reap() {
471	    local pid="${_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID:-}"
472	    [[ -n "$pid" ]] || return 0
473	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
474	    if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
475	        kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
476	        local i
477	        for (( i = 0; i < ${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_REAP_TIMEOUT:-45} * 10; i++ )); do
478	            kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
479	            sleep 0.1
480	        done
481	        kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
482	    fi
483	    wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
484	    return 0
485	}

487	# ─── _runner_now_short (#508) — HH:MM:SS UTC for stage banners ───────────────
488	# Returns ??:??:?? UTC when the underlying clock primitive yields nothing
489	# (defensive — the operator-visible banner still renders without crashing).
490	_runner_now_short() {
491	    local ms; ms="$(_runner_now_ms)"
492	    if [[ -z "$ms" || ! "$ms" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
493	        printf '??:??:?? UTC'
494	        return 0
495	    fi
496	    local sec=$(( ms / 1000 ))
497	    local out
498	    out="$(date -u -r "$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
499	        || date -u -d "@$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
500	        || printf '??:??:?? UTC')"
501	    printf '%s' "$out"
502	}

504	# ─── _runner_duration_token <stage> (#508) ───────────────────────────────────
505	# Format the elapsed duration since the start cache was populated. Mirrors
506	# stage-io.sh::_stage_io_render_duration's "<N.N>s" for sub-minute durations;
507	# for >= 60 s we use "<m>m<ss>s" so a slow stage doesn't render as "127.4s".
508	# Cache miss → "?s" (no crash).
509	_runner_duration_token() {
510	    local stage="$1"
511	    local start="${_RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS[$stage]:-}"
512	    if [[ -z "$start" || ! "$start" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
513	        printf '?s'
514	        return 0
515	    fi
516	    local now; now="$(_runner_now_ms)"
517	    if [[ -z "$now" || ! "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
518	        printf '?s'
519	        return 0
520	    fi
521	    local ms=$(( now - start ))
522	    (( ms < 0 )) && ms=0
523	    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
524	        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'
525	    else
526	        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
527	        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
528	        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))
529	        printf '%dm%02ds' "$mins" "$secs"
530	    fi
531	}

533	# ─── _runner_export_scope_allowlist <state_dir> (ADR-043) ────────────────────
534	# Redaction by construction: the per-run scope allowlist, exported as
535	# ZBUILD_SCOPE_ALLOWLIST so route_to_model can redact without a plugin passing
536	# it. Called per-stage because nothing is reported before plan runs (empty then —
537	# harmless, the scope manifest is the base allowlist and this is purely ADDITIVE).

539	    local state_dir="$1"
540	    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json" csv=""
541	    # #2189: the scope files stages REPORTED (plan reports its files) — the
542	    # engine no longer reads plan.json by path.
543	    if [[ -s "$rec" ]]; then
544	        csv="$(jq -r '(.scope_files // []) | unique | join(",")' "$rec" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
545	    fi

547	    # so build, redaction and shape-floor all read one list that already holds

554	        fi

556	            local -a _scope_arr=() ; local _ff
557	            IFS=',' read -r -a _scope_arr <<< "$csv"

559	                [[ -n "$_ff" && ",$_RUNNER_FLOOR_CSV," != *",$_ff,"* ]] && _RUNNER_FLOOR_CSV+=",$_ff"
560	            done < <(sf_scope_floor_files "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-$PWD}" "${_scope_arr[@]}" 2>/dev/null)

567	# ─── _runner_record_report <state_dir> <stage> <report-json> (#2189) ─────────
568	# Merge one dispatch's report into the run's record, artifacts/stage-reports.json
569	# (under artifacts/ so it is snapshotted and restored with the run): scope and
570	# wiring files are unioned; owned files are kept per reporting stage, so the
571	# deny list can exempt the owner. Engine setup reads THIS record — never a
572	# stage's artifact by name. Best-effort: a failed merge leaves the prior record.
573	# Parallel members record concurrently, so the read-merge-write holds a mkdir
574	# lock (portable; flock is absent on stock macOS) — else a sibling's merge is lost.
575	# A lock left by a killed holder is reclaimed after 10s.
576	_runner_record_report() {
577	    local state_dir="$1" stage="$2" report="${3:-}"
578	    [[ -n "$state_dir" && -n "$stage" && -n "$report" && "$report" != "{}" ]] || return 0
579	    # Most stages report none of the setup fields — skip the lock and the jq fork.
580	    [[ "$report" == *'"scope_files"'* || "$report" == *'"owned_files"'* \
581	        || "$report" == *'"wiring_files"'* ]] || return 0
582	    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json" tmp
583	    local lock="$state_dir/.stage-reports.lock" _tries=0
584	    [[ -d "$state_dir/artifacts" ]] || mkdir -p "$state_dir/artifacts" 2>/dev/null || return 0
585	    until mkdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; do
586	        # A merge takes milliseconds; a lock held 10s belongs to a dead holder.
587	        if (( ++_tries > 200 )); then rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; _tries=0; fi
588	        sleep 0.05
589	    done
590	    [[ -s "$rec" ]] || printf '{}' > "$rec"
591	    tmp="$rec.tmp.$BASHPID"
592	    if jq --arg s "$stage" --argjson r "$report" '
593	            .scope_files  = ((.scope_files  // []) + ($r.scope_files  // []) | unique)
594	          | .wiring_files = ((.wiring_files // []) + ($r.wiring_files // []) | unique)
595	          | if ($r.owned_files // null) != null
596	              then .owned_files = ((.owned_files // {}) + {($s): ($r.owned_files | unique)})
597	              else . end' "$rec" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
598	        mv -f "$tmp" "$rec"
599	    else
600	        rm -f "$tmp"
601	    fi
602	    rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null
603	    return 0
604	}

606	# ─── _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability <stages_arr_name> <plugins_root> ─────
607	# ADR-047 §5: the manifest-derived membership fence — the sole membership
608	# enforcement (the old hardcoded-roster fence is deleted, #1299). Every leaf in the
609	# resolved template flow must resolve to a plugin via resolve_stage_plugin
610	# (role-then-id, ADR-042); an unresolved leaf names the id.
611	#
612	# It is a CONTRACT check, so it is gated by the SAME ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR mode
613	# the inter-stage contract-validator uses (they must agree). Load-time membership
614	# enforcement is the ENFORCE-mode job; the opt-out modes (warn/off) skip it — so
615	# this preflight is a TRUE NO-OP whenever enforcement is off and never perturbs the
616	# mock-roster suites that drive runner.sh under warn (they resolve their leaves at
617	# dispatch via mocked plugin_hook_call, not through a real registry):
618	#   - enforce (default, real runs) / unset → ERROR fail-closed (rc=2). This is the
619	#     load-time guarantee that replaces the old canonical membership gate.
620	#   - warn / off (or any unknown mode)     → skip. Dispatch-time resolution
621	#     (resolve_stage_plugin in the stage loop) still fails a genuinely-missing
622	#     plugin mid-run — the backstop for opt-out runs.
623	# Takes the stage array BY NAME to avoid a subshell copy on read.
624	_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability() {
625	    local _arr_name="$1" plugins_root="$2"
626	    # Only enforce gates at load; warn/off/unknown are opt-outs → no-op. (The
627	    # default is enforce, matching contract-validator's default; unknown modes
628	    # degrade to non-enforce, exactly as contract-validator degrades them to warn.)
629	    [[ "${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-enforce}" == "enforce" ]] || return 0
630	    # Validate the array name is a plain identifier before binding the nameref
631	    # below — never bind a name assembled from unvalidated input (Copilot #1290:
632	    # injection footgun). Callers pass a literal ("active_stages"), so a
633	    # non-identifier is a programming error, not runtime data.
634	    if [[ ! "$_arr_name" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]]; then
635	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: invalid array name '${_arr_name}'"
636	        return 1
637	    fi
638	    # bash errors on a nameref that resolves to itself; reject it with our own
639	    # message rather than a raw "circular name reference" from the shell.
640	    if [[ "$_arr_name" == "_stages" ]]; then
641	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: array name '_stages' collides with the nameref"
642	        return 1
643	    fi
644	    # Warm the manifest cache in THIS shell before resolving anything. Every
645	    # resolution below reads manifests through `$( )`, and an associative-array
646	    # write inside a command substitution dies with that subshell — so a lazily
647	    # filled cache is never inherited (#1614, the reason yaml_cache_prewarm
648	    # exists and main() calls it at line ~1370).
649	    #
650	    # main() is not the only entry point. Tests source this file and call helpers
651	    # directly, never reaching that prewarm, and then every lookup forks awk:
652	    # template-resolvability-preflight-test.sh made 28,068 yaml_get calls with
653	    # ZERO cache hits, at real 150s / user 52s / sys 81s — kernel time 1.55x
654	    # user, which is process creation, not computation. Prewarming here took it
655	    # to 82.75s with sys 81s -> 45s.
656	    #
657	    # Here and not in setup_test_env: the prewarm costs 1.32s, and 570 test
658	    # files would pay ~747s for it to benefit the few that resolve plugins.
659	    # Measured before choosing the seam.
660	    #
661	    # Idempotent: a second call re-reads the same keys, which are now cache
662	    # hits. Cheap no-op in production, where main() has already warmed it.
663	    if declare -F yaml_cache_prewarm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
664	        yaml_cache_prewarm "$plugins_root"
665	    fi
666	    # Discovery too, for the same reason and in the same shell: it validates
667	    # every manifest on every call (~1.47s even with the yaml cache warm) and
668	    # runs once per leaf. 19 leaves x 2 templates was 38 full re-validations of
669	    # an unchanged tree.
670	    if declare -F discover_plugins >/dev/null 2>&1; then
671	        discover_plugins "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
672	    fi
673	    local -n _stages="${_arr_name}"
674	    local _leaf _ok=1
675	    for _leaf in "${_stages[@]+"${_stages[@]}"}"; do
676	        [[ -z "$_leaf" ]] && continue
677	        # A cycle/parallel GROUP id is a composition operator, not a leaf, and is
678	        # not itself a plugin — its members are already flattened into the stage
679	        # list. Skip group ids (their _TPL_STAGE_TYPE_<id> is cycle|parallel).
680	        local _t_var="_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_${_leaf//-/_}"
681	        case "${!_t_var:-leaf}" in
682	            cycle|parallel) continue ;;
683	        esac
684	        if ! resolve_stage_plugin "$_leaf" "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
685	            error "load_template: stage '${_leaf}' resolves to no plugin (ADR-047 §5: every leaf must resolve via role or id; add a plugin whose provides.role matches, or whose id is '${_leaf}')"
686	            _ok=0
687	        fi
688	    done
689	    [[ $_ok -eq 1 ]]
690	}

692	# ─── _runner_validate_startup_preflight [violation_fixture] (ADR-051 §warn-first) ──
693	# Aggregation SKELETON (#1318 / D1): owns the violations[]/fail_count collection,
694	# the render-all-at-once block (same pattern as _contract_validate_pipeline) and the
695	# warn/enforce/off mode dispatch. Separate gate from _runner_validate_leaf_
696	# resolvability — it covers non-contract elements the DAG validator does not address.
697	#
698	# It deliberately contributes NO checks of its own yet. The concrete producers land
699	# downstream, each against the discriminating fixtures #1605 pre-stages:
700	#   - persona-binding existence (PERSONA_MISSING) → #1320 (D3)
701	#   - requires.plugins resolution (PLUGIN_MISSING) → #1321 (D4)
702	# An earlier draft carried both checks here, untested; the requires.plugins one was
703	# an acknowledged approximation that raised spurious PLUGIN_MISSING for any entry
704	# naming an ordinary plugin. Shipping checks no test discriminates is the green-but-
705	# inert shape #1605 exists to prevent, so they were removed rather than carried.
706	#
707	# Deliberate divergence from _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: the DEFAULT mode
708	# here is WARN (not enforce). This lands warn-first so operators see failures before
709	# enforcement is mandatory. Set ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=enforce to fail-closed.
710	# ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=off is a full no-op (skips all checks, emits nothing).
711	#
712	# The optional first argument is a synthetic violation fixture: it injects one
713	# pre-formed violation so the aggregation, rendering and mode dispatch are testable
714	# before any real producer exists. A non-empty string yields exactly one violation;
715	# empty (or omitted) yields none. Runtime call sites in runner.sh pass no argument,
716	# so until D3/D4 land the live path always renders nothing and returns 0.
717	# shellcheck disable=SC2120  # $1 is used by unit tests; runtime call sites pass no arg
718	_runner_validate_startup_preflight() {
719	    local _violation_fixture="${1:-}"
720	    local mode="${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-warn}"
721	    case "$mode" in
722	        warn|enforce|off) ;;
723	        *) mode="warn" ;;
724	    esac
725	
726	    # off = complete no-op, no output
727	    [[ "$mode" == "off" ]] && return 0
728	
729	    local -a violations=()
730	    local fail_count=0
731	
732	    # Synthetic violation fixture for unit tests — non-empty arg injects one violation.
733	    if [[ -n "$_violation_fixture" ]]; then
734	        violations+=("${_violation_fixture}|SYNTHETIC|fixture|synthetic violation injected by test fixture")
735	        fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
736	    fi
737	
738	    # Check producers append to violations[]/fail_count here — see #1320 (persona
739	    # binding) and #1321 (requires.plugins). Until one lands, the only source of a

801	    local start="${_RUNNER_PIPELINE_START_MS:-}"
802	    if [[ -z "$start" || ! "$start" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
803	        printf '?s'
804	        return 0
805	    fi
806	    local now; now="$(_runner_now_ms)"
807	    if [[ -z "$now" || ! "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
808	        printf '?s'

810	    fi
811	    local ms=$(( now - start ))
812	    (( ms < 0 )) && ms=0
813	    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
814	        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'
815	    else
816	        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
817	        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
818	        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))

861	# ─── _render_pipeline_end <status> [stage] [rc] (#525) ───────────────────────
862	# Emits the terminal banner that closes a pipeline run, framed with ═ (U+2550)
863	# to distinguish the pipeline boundary from the stage divider (━) and stage-io
864	# banners (─). Two-line layout:
865	#
866	#   ════════════════ pipeline.end ════════════════ HH:MM:SS UTC
867	#   <glyph> Pipeline <status_word>: status=<X> run_id=<Y> issue=<N> (took <dur>)
868	#
869	# Frame bars colored BLUE (chrome). Glyph + leading status word inherit the
870	# verdict class color (foreground signal). Right-aligned timestamp via the
871	# same width math as _render_stage_divider — degrades to a symmetric divider
872	# (no timestamp) when mid_bar <= 2.
873	#
874	# Writes to fd 2 so it composes correctly with other operator lines (info /
875	# success / error) under the same output redirection rules. Banner is emitted
876	# AFTER the pipeline.end JSONL event so the durable event is fail-closed
877	# against banner-write failures.
878	_render_pipeline_end() {
879	    local status="${1:-unknown}"
880	    local stage_hint="${2:-}"
881	    local rc_hint="${3:-}"
882	    local run_id="${_runner_run_id:-?}"
883	    local issue="${_runner_issue:-?}"
884	    # Best-effort value gathering. Each `$(...)` here forks a helper that may
885	    # itself fork an external (awk in the duration token, date/tput in the
886	    # clock/width helpers). Most call sites invoke this banner DIRECTLY under the
887	    # runner's `set -e` (e.g. the cycle/stage abort + LLM/scope-abort paths) —
888	    # not wrapped in `|| true` — so a transient under-load fork failure in any
889	    # one of these bare assignments would trip errexit and abort the render
890	    # BEFORE the printf block, silently dropping the operator's terminal banner
891	    # mid-teardown. `|| fallback` neutralizes errexit at each assignment so the
892	    # banner is always emitted once the function is reached, on every call site.
893	    # (#1156)
894	    local dur; dur="$(_runner_pipeline_duration_token)" || dur='?s'
895	    local glyph; glyph="$(_pipeline_status_glyph "$status")" || glyph='✗'
896	    local color; color="$(_pipeline_status_color "$status")" || color=''
897	    local frame="${BLUE:-}"
898	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)" || ts='??:??:?? UTC'
899	    local width; width="$(_term_width)" || width=80
900	
901	    # Map status → operator-friendly verb for line 2. Tracks event payload
902	    # verbatim so "status=<X>" agrees with the verb. ("success" in legacy
903	    # event payloads renders as "complete" — see ADR-015 §v5 amendment).
904	    local word
905	    case "$status" in
906	        success|complete)        word="complete" ;;
907	        complete_unconverged)    word="complete_unconverged" ;;
908	        failed)                  word="failed" ;;
909	        interrupted)             word="interrupted" ;;
910	        aborted)                 word="aborted" ;;
911	        preflight_failed)        word="preflight_failed" ;;
912	        *)                       word="$status" ;;
913	    esac
914	
915	    local label=" pipeline.end "
916	    # Layout: <left_bar><label><mid_bar> <ts>
917	    local left_bar=$(( (width - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1) / 2 ))
918	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))
919	
920	    local detail_status="status=${status}"
921	    [[ -n "$stage_hint" ]] && detail_status+=" stage=${stage_hint}"
922	    [[ -n "$rc_hint"    ]] && detail_status+=" rc=${rc_hint}"
923	
924	    if [[ "$mid_bar" -le 2 ]]; then
925	        # Degraded layout — drop timestamp from the header.
926	        local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
927	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
928	        local bar
929	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
930	        bar="${bar// /═}"
931	        {
932	            printf '\n'
933	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$frame" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$frame" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
934	            printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
935	                "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
936	                "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
937	        } >&2
938	        _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
939	        return 0
940	    fi
941	
942	    local lbar rbar
943	    printf -v lbar '%*s' "$left_bar" ''; lbar="${lbar// /═}"
944	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /═}"
945	    {
946	        printf '\n'
947	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
948	            "$frame" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
949	            "$frame" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"
950	        printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
951	            "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
952	            "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
953	    } >&2
954	    _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
955	}

972	# ─── _render_stage_divider <stage> (#492, ts: #508) ──────────────────────────
973	# Emits a blank line + a heavy horizontal rule (━ U+2501) with the stage name
974	# centered in stage-color, then another blank line — written to fd 2 so it
975	# survives the same redirection rules as ▸/✓/✗ info lines. Used on every
976	# stage transition (between eb_emit_event "stage.start" and "▸ Running stage")
977	# so the operator's eye finds the next stage boundary at a glance.
978	#
979	# #508: right-align an HH:MM:SS UTC timestamp on the divider, mirroring the
980	# stage-io banner header right-alignment (_stage_io_compose_banner). Width
981	# math (no bookend glyphs in this layout — just bars + label + sep + ts):
982	#   visible = left_bar + len(label) + mid_bar + 1 (space) + len(ts)
983	#   left_bar = (width - len(label) - len(ts) - 1) / 2
984	#   mid_bar  = width - left_bar - len(label) - len(ts) - 1
985	# Degrade rule: when mid_bar <= 2 (very narrow terminals) we drop the
986	# timestamp and emit the legacy symmetric divider so layout stays legible.
987	_render_stage_divider() {
988	    local stage="$1"
989	    local width
990	    width="$(_term_width)"
991	    local color
992	    color="$(_stage_color "$stage")"
993	    local label=" ${stage} "
994	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)"
995	
996	    # Layout: <left_bar><label><mid_bar> <ts>
997	    # Visible width = left_bar + len(label) + mid_bar + 1 (sep) + len(ts).
998	    local left_bar=$(( (width - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1) / 2 ))
999	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))
1000	
1001	    if [[ "$mid_bar" -le 2 ]]; then
1002	        # Degraded: legacy symmetric divider, no timestamp (narrow terminal).
1003	        local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1004	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1005	        local bar
1006	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1007	        bar="${bar// /━}"
1008	        {
1009	            printf '\n'
1010	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$color" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$color" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1011	            printf '\n'
1012	            # #523: trailing blank line — combined with the existing leading
1013	            # \n above, produces two stacked blanks between consecutive stages.
1014	            # Cycle sub-dividers (ADR-015 §v6) intentionally do NOT add this.
1015	            printf '\n'
1016	        } >&2
1017	        return 0
1018	    fi
1019	
1020	    local lbar rbar
1021	    printf -v lbar '%*s' "$left_bar" ''; lbar="${lbar// /━}"
1022	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /━}"
1023	    {
1024	        printf '\n'
1025	        # %b on colored fragments so \033[...] resolves like echo -e elsewhere.
1026	        # Timestamp is plain text outside color escapes — NO_COLOR keeps it.
1027	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
1028	            "$color" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1029	            "$color" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"
1030	        printf '\n'
1031	        # #523: trailing blank line — combined with the leading \n above,
1032	        # produces two stacked blanks between consecutive stages. Cycle
1033	        # sub-dividers (ADR-015 §v6) intentionally do NOT add this.
1034	        printf '\n'
1035	    } >&2
1036	}

1040	# hierarchy that nests cleanly with the existing stage-transition divider
1041	# (_render_stage_divider) so the operator can see cycle entry, per-iter
1042	# boundaries, per-iter outcomes, and cycle exit in the scrollback.
1043	#
1044	# Glyph + color ladder (heaviest → lightest):
1045	#   ━━━ (U+2501) stage transition   — BOLD BLUE (handled in _render_stage_divider)

1177	    {
1178	        printf '%b↳ iter %s complete: verdict=%s score=%s failure_count=%s elapsed=%ss%b\n' \
1179	            "${DIM:-}" "$iter" "$verdict" "$score" "$failure_count" "$elapsed_s" "${RESET:-}"
1180	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1181	}
1182	
1183	# ─── _render_cycle_exit <cycle_id> <reason> <iter> <max> ──────────────────────
1184	# Heavy `═` LIGHT_BLUE divider + verdict-glyph line mapping termination reason
1185	# to glyph + color (see #524 spec).
1186	#   converged       → ✓ GREEN+BOLD
1187	#   max_iterations  → ✗ RED+BOLD
1188	#   plateau         → ✗ RED+BOLD
1189	#   divergence      → ✗ RED+BOLD
1190	#   aborted         → ⚠ YELLOW+BOLD
1191	#   verdict_missing → ⚠ YELLOW+BOLD
1192	#   blocked         → ✗ RED+BOLD (sibling #528)
1193	#   error/config_invalid → ✗ RED+BOLD
1194	#   unknown (typo)  → ✗ RED+BOLD (fail loud)
1195	# Emitted by the runner AFTER cycle_orchestrator_run via _cycle_handle_terminal.
1196	_render_cycle_exit() {
1197	    local cycle_id="$1" reason="$2" iter="$3" max="$4"
1198	    local glyph color text
1199	    case "$reason" in
1200	        converged)
1201	            glyph="✓"; color="${GREEN:-}"
1202	            text="Cycle ${cycle_id} converged in ${iter}/${max} iters"
1203	            ;;
1204	        max_iterations)
1205	            glyph="✗"; color="${RED:-}"
1206	            text="Cycle ${cycle_id} exhausted max_iterations (${iter}/${max})"
1207	            ;;
1208	        plateau)
1209	            glyph="✗"; color="${RED:-}"
1210	            text="Cycle ${cycle_id} halted: plateau"
1211	            ;;
1212	        divergence)
1213	            glyph="✗"; color="${RED:-}"
1214	            text="Cycle ${cycle_id} halted: divergence"
1215	            ;;
1216	        aborted)
1217	            glyph="⚠"; color="${YELLOW:-}"
1218	            text="Cycle ${cycle_id} aborted: ${reason}"
1219	            ;;
1220	        verdict_missing)
1221	            glyph="⚠"; color="${YELLOW:-}"
1222	            text="Cycle ${cycle_id} halted: verdict missing"
1223	            ;;
1224	        blocked)
1225	            glyph="✗"; color="${RED:-}"
1226	            text="Cycle ${cycle_id} halted: blocked"
1227	            ;;
1228	        blocked_on_scope)
1229	            # #840: build needs out-of-scope files the policy won't grant.
1230	            glyph="⚠"; color="${YELLOW:-}"
1231	            text="Cycle ${cycle_id} halted: blocked on scope (needs files outside write-scope)"
