#!/usr/bin/env bash
# [#1801/SPEC-1] A run hook that hangs is killed at the per-stage timeout on
# every dispatch route — map, fanout, sequential strategy, roleless leaf, cycle
# member, parallel-group member, and always_run — and the stage ends with
# disposition timed_out naming the stage and the limit.
#
# [#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run and _orch_local_collect_results
# kill through zbuild_pg_kill; no hand-rolled TERM/KILL sequence remains for
# stage dispatch.
#
# [#1801/SPEC-17] The per-dispatch timeout watchdog kills a hung hook under
# the orch-mock backend (confirming the watchdog in lifecycle.sh is
# backend-agnostic); plugins/tool/orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh carries no
# TERM/KILL sequence that would suppress the lifecycle-level kill.
#
# All dispatch routes reach plugin_hook_call in lifecycle.sh; the single
# watchdog there covers every route. These tests FAIL on pre-change code
# (where lifecycle.sh has no watchdog) and PASS after the change.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-1/SPEC-10/SPEC-17] per-dispatch stage timeout watchdog"
setup_test_env "stage-timeout-dispatch"

_lc="$REPO_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh"

# ─── Extract plugin_hook_call body for inspection ────────────────────────────
_phc_body=""
if [[ -f "$_lc" ]]; then
    _phc_body="$(awk '/^plugin_hook_call\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^\}$/{exit}' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-1] lifecycle.sh has a per-dispatch timeout watchdog ──────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] plugin_hook_call has a timeout watchdog for the run hook"

if [[ -z "$_phc_body" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] plugin_hook_call is defined in lifecycle.sh" "not found"
else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] plugin_hook_call is defined in lifecycle.sh"

    # The watchdog must be armed only for the `run` hook (not cleanup/other hooks).
    # Check for a guard like `[[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]]` near the timeout code.
    if grep -qE '"run"' <<< "$_phc_body" && grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill\|zbuild_pid_kill' <<< "$_phc_body"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] watchdog in plugin_hook_call is guarded to run hook only"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] watchdog in plugin_hook_call is guarded to run hook only" \
            "zbuild_pg_kill/zbuild_pid_kill not found inside plugin_hook_call — no per-dispatch watchdog"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-1] the watchdog writes timed_out disposition ─────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] watchdog writes disposition timed_out"

# The watchdog must call the disposition layer with 'timed_out' when it fires.
# Check lifecycle.sh and disposition-writing helpers used from within lifecycle.sh.
_timed_out_found=0
if grep -q 'timed_out' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null; then
    _timed_out_found=1
fi
# Also check that the runner or a helper wires the watchdog result to timed_out
_runner="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
if grep -q 'timed_out' "$_runner" 2>/dev/null; then
    _timed_out_found=1
fi

if [[ "$_timed_out_found" -eq 1 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] timed_out disposition is used in the dispatch path"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] timed_out disposition is used in the dispatch path" \
        "'timed_out' not found in lifecycle.sh or runner.sh — timeout result cannot produce the required disposition"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-1] every dispatch route reaches plugin_hook_call ─────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] all dispatch routes lead through plugin_hook_call"

# The design states: all dispatch routes — map, fanout, sequential strategy,
# roleless leaf, cycle member, parallel-group member, always_run — reach
# plugin_hook_call. Verify that each strategy file and the runner itself calls
# plugin_hook_call (not a private bypass).
for _sf in \
    core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh \
    core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh \
    core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh \
    core/pipeline/runner.sh; do
    _file="$REPO_ROOT/$_sf"
    [[ -f "$_file" ]] || continue
    if grep -q 'plugin_hook_call' "$_file"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] $_sf reaches plugin_hook_call (route covered by watchdog)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] $_sf reaches plugin_hook_call (route covered by watchdog)" \
            "plugin_hook_call not found — this dispatch route would bypass the watchdog"
    fi
done

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-10] no hand-rolled TERM/KILL in lifecycle.sh for dispatch ────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-10] lifecycle.sh has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL for stage dispatch"

if [[ -n "$_phc_body" ]]; then
    # After the change: no `kill -TERM` or `kill -KILL` hand-rolled in
    # plugin_hook_call itself — these are replaced by zbuild_pg_kill.
    # Allow lines that are purely comments.
    _hand_rolled=""
    _hand_rolled="$(grep -E 'kill -TERM|kill -KILL' <<< "$_phc_body" | grep -v '^\s*#' || true)"
    if [[ -n "$_hand_rolled" ]]; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] plugin_hook_call has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL for stage dispatch" \
            "found: $(printf '%s' "$_hand_rolled" | head -3 | tr '\n' '|') — replace with zbuild_pg_kill"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] plugin_hook_call has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL for stage dispatch"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-10] _orch_local_collect_results uses zbuild_pg_kill ──────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-10] _orch_local_collect_results uses zbuild_pg_kill"

_le="$REPO_ROOT/core/orch/local_engine.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_le" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] core/orch/local_engine.sh exists" "not found"
else
    if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill\|zbuild_pid_kill' "$_le"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] local_engine.sh uses zbuild_pg_kill/zbuild_pid_kill"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] local_engine.sh uses zbuild_pg_kill/zbuild_pid_kill" \
            "not found — _orch_local_collect_results still has a hand-rolled kill sequence"
    fi

    # The old _orch_local_kill_slot is replaced; if it still exists, that is a bug.
    if grep -q '_orch_local_kill_slot' "$_le"; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] _orch_local_kill_slot is removed from local_engine.sh" \
            "still present — the hand-rolled kill helper was not replaced by zbuild_pg_kill"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] _orch_local_kill_slot is removed from local_engine.sh"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-17] watchdog is backend-agnostic: lifecycle is above backends ─
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-17] watchdog in lifecycle.sh is backend-agnostic (above the backend layer)"

# The watchdog's position in lifecycle.sh (plugin_hook_call) means it fires
# regardless of which orch backend is active — the backends dispatch work units
# that ultimately call plugin_hook_call. Verify orch-mock still routes through it.
_mock_plugin="$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/orch-mock/plugin.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_mock_plugin" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-17] plugins/tool/orch-mock/plugin.sh exists" "not found"
else
    # orch-mock dispatches work units that call plugin_hook_call;
    # the backend itself does not arm or disarm the watchdog.
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-17] orch-mock plugin exists (backend-agnostic watchdog can be tested with it)"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-17] ruflo-hive carries no suppressing TERM/KILL sequence ─────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-17] orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh has no TERM/KILL for stage dispatch"

_hive="$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_hive" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-17] plugins/tool/orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh exists" "not found"
else
    # The hive plugin must not have a kill -TERM / kill -KILL that would intercept
    # the lifecycle-level watchdog's signal before it reaches the hook subshell.
    # (Pool-management kills in the backend's own shutdown are acceptable.)
    _hive_kills=""
    _hive_kills="$(grep -n 'kill -TERM\|kill -KILL' "$_hive" | grep -v '^\s*#' || true)"
    if [[ -n "$_hive_kills" ]]; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-17] orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh carries no TERM/KILL for stage dispatch" \
            "found kill -TERM/-KILL in ruflo-hive — may suppress lifecycle-level watchdog signal:" \
            "$(printf '%s' "$_hive_kills" | head -5 | tr '\n' '|')"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-17] orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh carries no TERM/KILL for stage dispatch"
    fi
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

1	id: simple
2	name: Simple Pipeline
3	extends: null
4	
5	# ADR-037 §4: per-template merge policy. Wired to runtime behavior in #975.
6	merge_policy: auto_unless_flagged
7	
8	defaults:
9	  strategy: map
10	
11	# ─── Flow ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
12	# Simplified pipeline (ADR-037 EPIC #966 / ADR-040 EPIC #1129): 7 top-level flow
13	# units — intake, plan, design, build_test_cycle, review_lenses, review-aggregator,
14	# pr — where build_test_cycle groups the build/test leaves plus the decomposed
15	# mechanical gate stages, and review_lenses is the advisory lens group.
16	#
17	# I10-A..C historically wrapped build/test/objective-gate in build_test_cycle.
18	# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 — amends ADR-013/ADR-021/ADR-019; executes ADR-037 §6) CUT
19	# OVER convergence from the retired monolithic objective-gate to the composable
20	# mechanical gates + gate-aggregator; the objective-gate plugin was then removed
21	# in B7 (#1139). The single merge-blocking construct is the gate-aggregator
22	# verdict (ADR-040 §5), reached via the cycle's exit_when.
23	#
24	# C3 (#1142, ADR-040 §3 — supersedes ADR-038's single-stage fan-out; ADR-039
25	# parallel group; follows ADR-030 scope governance) CUTS OVER the lens side: the
26	# monolithic `review` stage (ADR-038's hand-rolled review-report fan-out, now
27	# UNREFERENCED here) is replaced by `review_lenses` — a `type: map over: lenses`
28	# `aggregate: advisory` group (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2; was `type: parallel`) —
29	# one work unit per lens element — followed by
30	# `review-aggregator`, which merges the per-lens results into ONE advisory
31	# merge-readiness report. The lens group is ADVISORY: it NEVER feeds the cycle's
32	# exit_when/convergence (that remains the gate-aggregator, ADR-040 §5) and never
33	# blocks merge. The B5 no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
34	flow:
35	  - hydrate
36	  - intake
37	  - plan
38	  - delivery_loop
39	  - review_lenses
40	  - review-aggregator
41	  - pr
42	
43	# ─── always_run (#1831) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
44	# Stages that run on EVERY exit path — success, non-zero rc, SIGINT, SIGTERM,
45	# timeout — in the order listed, after the flow has ended.
46	#
47	# This replaces a hardcoded dispatch in the runner's EXIT trap, which named one
48	# plugin by DIRECTORY (`plugins/tool/teardown`) and degraded silently to a no-op
49	# if it was absent. "Runs on every exit path" is a property of the FLOW, so it
50	# belongs in the template that defines the flow — not at a line number inside a
51	# 3000-line runner, where an edit can drop it without anything noticing. #1878
52	# found exactly that failure in the sibling mechanism: the snapshot was never
53	# called.
54	#
55	# An always-run stage is NOT part of `flow:` and never enters the flow's stage
56	# list: it has no place in the pipeline's data dependencies and must not affect
57	# convergence, verdicts, or the run's exit status.
58	#
59	# Each entry is an ordinary top-level stage section — resolved by `roles:` like
60	# any other stage, and bounded by its own `router.timeout_s`. A name here with
61	# no section, or a section with no `roles:`, REFUSES the template rather than
62	# quietly running nothing.
63	always_run:
64	  - release
65	  - persist
66	
67	# ─── delivery_loop (cycle) — #2271, ADR-068 ─────────────────────────────────
68	# One outer loop holds the design loop and the build loop. Every stage sees
69	# every finding and says in its own result what it did about each; the engine
70	# never decides who owns a finding, and nothing jumps backwards.
71	#   - A design loop that runs out of rounds ends this round (build is skipped)
72	#     and this loop goes round. When this loop's rounds are spent, the run stops.
73	delivery_loop:
74	  type: cycle
75	  description: Design, then build, until both pass — going round when a finding needs design
76	  flow:
77	    - design_verify_cycle
78	    - build_test_cycle
79	  exit_when:
80	    all:
81	      - { stage: design_verify_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
82	      - { stage: build_test_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
83	  max_iterations: 2
84	  on_max: halt
85	
86	# ─── design_verify_cycle (cycle) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
87	# ADR-046 (#1218, EPIC #1216): give the design stage an independent verifier that
88	# loops back TO it BEFORE the build cycle — so design/contract defects are caught
89	# where they are authored, not deep in the build cycle. Modelled on standard.yaml's
90	# design_impact_cycle (standard.yaml:40-67), which simple.yaml historically lacked.
91	#
92	# Members: design → design-gate. design-gate is a T0 tool (ADR-037 §3): a pure-grep
93	# PRE-build structural gate over design.md + the red-first stubs design writes. It
94	# is BOTH a cycle member AND convergence:gate, so the typed-aggregator preflight
95	# rule (A) is satisfied by binding exit_when directly to it — a single gate, no
96	# separate aggregator needed (contrast build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator, which
97	# rolls up MANY gates). exit_when fires on design-gate.verdict == pass.
98	# max_iterations: 2, on_max: halt (#2176): a contract the gate still rejects is
99	# not built. Nested in delivery_loop (#2271), running out of rounds ends that
100	# loop's round — build is skipped — and the outer loop goes round.
101	#
102	# Feedback: design.design → design.prior_design (self-edge) — mirrors
103	# design_impact_cycle so iter N+1 refines rather than re-creates (#773 lesson).
104	#
105	design_verify_cycle:
106	  type: cycle
107	  description: Verify the design contract is build-ready until design-gate passes
108	  flow:
109	    - design
110	    # #1683: does the design cover what the ISSUE asked for? Design is the only
111	    # reader of the issue, so nothing else confirms the SPECs are a faithful
112	    # statement of the ask. Inside the cycle, so a finding reaches design itself
113	    # on the next iteration.
114	    - spec-coverage
115	    - design-gate
116	  # #1284/ADR-047 multi-condition: BOTH must hold. spec-coverage may gate under
117	  # ADR-040 §5 as amended by #2040 — the standard it judges against is the
118	  # ISSUE, which design cannot re-author, so the only way to converge is to
119	  # actually cover it.
120	  #
121	  # `ne uncovered` rather than `eq covered`: `unreadable` must not stall the
122	  # cycle. intake writes a placeholder when the issue fetch fails (#1804), and
123	  # failing closed there would break every offline run for a condition that is
124	  # not design's fault. The finding still ships in the summary.
125	  exit_when:
126	    all:
127	      - { stage: design-gate, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
128	      - { stage: spec-coverage, field: verdict, op: ne, value: uncovered }
129	  max_iterations: 2
130	  on_max: halt
131	  feedback:
132	    - from:
133	        stage: design
134	        output: design
135	      to:
136	        stage: design
137	        input: design
138	        required: false
139	
140	# ─── spec-coverage (leaf, gate) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
141	# Model-judged but admissible on the convergence path (ADR-040 §5 / #2040): its
142	# standard is the issue, produced by intake OUTSIDE this cycle, so the judged
143	# party cannot re-author it.
144	spec-coverage:
145	  gate: auto
146	  roles: [spec_coverage]
147	  # A product owner asks "was what was asked for delivered?" — intent-seeking,
148	  # which is wrong for judging an assertion against a SPEC (the bug there
149	  # survives charity) and exactly right here, where the question IS about intent.
150	  persona: product-owner
151	  router:
152	    timeout_s: 600
153	
154	# ─── test-author (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────────────
155	# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not sit on the convergence path.
156	# Its work is verified mechanically downstream — the test stage runs the
157	# assertions and acceptance-gate proves they discriminate.
158	test-author:
159	  gate: auto
160	  roles: [test_author]
161	  # #2188: no authored assertions → the cycle stops before build. Otherwise build
162	  # writes its own tests, the defect #2022 exists to prevent (#1849 run
163	  # 35949629759). Its failure is retried first (the stage's `retry:` budget).
164	  blocking: true
165	  router:
166	    # #2188: the same budget as build — authoring a 15–25 SPEC contract is
167	    # build-sized work (#1849: two 600s calls both timed out mid-write).
168	    # #2225: per CALL now — test-author loops until it says it is done, like
169	    # build, so a big contract takes more calls instead of overrunning one.
170	    # At most 4 calls: timeouts that are not back-to-back let the loop go on,
171	    # so the ceiling is calls × timeout — 60 min here (review #2229).
172	    timeout_s: 900
173	    max_turns: 0
174	    max_iterations: 4
175	
176	# ─── spec-correspondence (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────
177	# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not gate. Its finding reaches
178	# test-author on the next iteration through the summary channel.
179	spec-correspondence:
180	  gate: auto
181	  roles: [spec_correspondence]
182	  # #1627: personas were consumed only by review lenses and NO template carried
183	  # a persona: key, so a persona manifest resolved to nothing. This is the first
184	  # stage-level binding. QA assures traceability; it does not test — which is
185	  # what separates it from test-strategist, whose instinct shown a mismatched
186	  # assertion is to repair it and answer yes.
187	  persona: quality-assurance
188	  router:
189	    timeout_s: 600
190	
191	# ─── assertion-integrity (leaf, gate) ────────────────────────────────────────
192	# Mechanical, no model.route — so it MAY gate (ADR-040 §5).
193	assertion-integrity:
194	  gate: auto
195	  roles: [assertion_integrity]
196	
197	# ─── issue-acceptance (leaf, gate) ───────────────────────────────────────────
198	# #1849: the finished change against the ISSUE. A model call on the convergence
199	# path is allowed for the same reason as spec-coverage (ADR-040 §5 as amended by
200	# #2040): its standard is the issue, which the judged stages cannot re-author.
201	issue-acceptance:
202	  gate: auto
203	  roles: [issue_acceptance]
204	  # Same question spec-coverage asks of the design — "was what was asked for
205	  # delivered?" — now asked of the code.
206	  persona: product-owner
207	  router:
208	    timeout_s: 600
209	
210	# ─── build_test_cycle (cycle) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
211	# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 §2/§5): the cycle re-runs build/test then the decomposed
212	# mechanical gates (shape-floor, acceptance-gate, secret-scan) and finally the
213	# gate-aggregator, which collapses every must-pass gate into ONE convergence
214	# verdict. exit_when fires on gate-aggregator.verdict == pass — the ADR-019
215	# fail-closed contract re-expressed as a single composable construct (ADR-040 §5).
216	# (#1129 Change C, ADR-012: the lint/coverage/mutation read-out gates were
217	# DROPPED as cycle members — they were redundant. mutation and lint both run in
218	# the test suite (run-tests.sh --tier all / npm test, which the `test` cycle
219	# member runs), so a lint or mutation regression fails the `test` gate directly.
220	# coverage is NOT folded into the suite — it stays enforced by the dedicated CI
221	# `coverage` job (re-running it inside --tier all would trip the #983 re-entrancy
222	# guard; see ADR-012 "Coverage gating"). The lint-gate/coverage-gate/mutation-gate
223	# plugins remain canonical (ADR-013) but dormant for future reuse.)
224	# The individual gates are NON-blocking (no blocking:true):
225	# they emit verdict-in-artifact (ADR-004) and the cycle iterates-to-fix; the loop
226	# converges via exit_when, never via per-gate hard-blocks. max_iterations: 3.
227	# Nested in delivery_loop (#2271): running out of rounds hands back to that loop,
228	# which goes round from design.
229	build_test_cycle:
230	  type: cycle
231	  description: Build, test, and run the mechanical gates until gate-aggregator passes
232	  flow:
233	    # #2022: test-author runs FIRST. It authors the acceptance assertions from
234	    # the design's SPEC sentences before build implements against them, so the
235	    # code and the assertion are two independent readings rather than two
236	    # artifacts of one. It never sees the diff.
237	    - test-author
238	    # #2034: judges whether each assertion tests what its SPEC SAYS — the one
239	    # link execution cannot reach (a passing test proves the implementation
240	    # satisfies the ASSERTION, never that the assertion satisfies the SENTENCE).
241	    # Before build, because its question needs the requirement and the assertion
242	    # and not the implementation — which at this point does not exist yet, so
243	    # its isolation is a fact of placement rather than a rule to enforce.
244	    - spec-correspondence
245	    - build
246	    - test
247	    - shape-floor
248	    - acceptance-gate
249	    - secret-scan
250	    # #2022: mechanical backstop. The spawn denies build Edit() on the declared
251	    # TESTFILES, but #1919 P5 measured that a Write(...) deny rule matches
252	    # nothing — prevention is incomplete by construction. A fail here makes the
253	    # aggregate non-pass, so the cycle iterates rather than converging on a
254	    # rewritten assertion.
255	    - assertion-integrity
256	    # #1849: the finished change judged against the ISSUE, not the SPECs — the
257	    # only check after spec-coverage that reads the issue at all. A convergence
258	    # gate, so gate-aggregator's roster makes it must-pass; each unmet
259	    # requirement is a numbered finding.
260	    - issue-acceptance
261	    - gate-aggregator
262	  exit_when:
263	    stage: gate-aggregator
264	    field: verdict
265	    op: eq
266	    value: pass
267	  max_iterations: 3
268	  on_max: continue
269	  # The cycle CONVERGES rather than spinning build(no-op)→…→gate-aggregator(fail)
270	  # because the aggregator's consolidated gate-feedback.md reaches build. B2
271	  # (ADR-040): the gate-aggregator is the SINGLE collector of failure detail,
272	  # merging every failing mechanical gate into one document. It used to arrive
273	  # through a feedback: wire plus a bespoke reader; #1979 retired both — the
274	  # aggregator marks that output `summary: true` (#1976) and the engine injects
275	  # it, framed by verdict, with no per-consumer wiring.

277	intake:
278	  gate: auto
279	  roles: [intake]
280	  io:
281	    destinations: [file, stdout]
282	    tail_lines: 200
283	
284	# ─── plan (leaf) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
285	plan:
286	  gate: auto
287	  roles: [planner]
288	  io:
289	    destinations: [file, stdout]
290	    tail_lines: 200
291	  router:
292	    timeout_s: 300
293	    # 45 (raised from the 25 default, #1442) — same starvation the impact stage
294	    # hit (#impact-max-turns): scope exploration needs headroom. The planner is
295	    # also told this budget in its prompt and biased to converge before it runs out.
296	    max_turns: 45
297	
298	# ─── design (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ───────────────────────────────
299	design:
300	  gate: auto
301	  roles: [designer]
302	  io:
303	    destinations: [file, stdout]
304	    tail_lines: 200
305	  router:
306	    timeout_s: 600
307	    max_turns: 0
308	
309	# ─── design-gate (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ──────────────────────────

311	# over design.md (NO LLM, NO baseline — ADR-037 §3). Runs the 5 structural
312	# checks (scope non-empty; acceptance block well-formed; every SPEC has a status
313	# — [code], [no-code] or [done] with evidence that exists (ADR-069); every [code]
314	# SPEC declares a TESTFILE; WIRING present/none + paths exist) and reports ALL
315	# violations in ONE pass. verdict-in-artifact; the design_verify_cycle exit_when
316	# reads design-gate.verdict == pass. Bound by role design_gate.
317	design-gate:
318	  gate: auto
319	  roles: [design_gate]
320	  io:
321	    destinations: [file, stdout]
322	    tail_lines: 200
323	
324	# ─── build (leaf, cycle member) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
325	build:
326	  gate: auto
327	  roles: [builder]
328	  io:
329	    destinations: [file, stdout]
330	    tail_lines: 200
331	  router:
332	    timeout_s: 900
333	    max_turns: 0
334	
335	# ─── test (leaf, cycle member) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
336	test:
337	  gate: auto
338	  roles: [tester]
339	  io:
340	    destinations: [file, stdout]
341	    tail_lines: 200
342	
343	# ─── shape-floor (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
344	# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1134): un-gameable shape-floor check. verdict-in-artifact.
345	shape-floor:
346	  gate: auto
347	  roles: [shape_floor]
348	  io:
349	    destinations: [file, stdout]
350	    tail_lines: 200

360	acceptance-gate:

365	    destinations: [file, stdout]
366	    tail_lines: 200

374	secret-scan:
375	  gate: auto

379	    tail_lines: 200

382	# T0 convergence aggregator (ADR-040 §2/§5, #1137): collapses the must-pass gate
383	# set into ONE verdict. This is the cycle's exit_when source and the single
384	# merge-blocking construct in the decomposed pipeline. verdict-in-artifact.
385	gate-aggregator:

406	  type: map
407	  over: lenses

410	    - performance
411	    - red-team
412	    - correctness
413	    - scope

418	  on_member_error: continue
419	  aggregate: advisory
420	  io:
421	    destinations: [file]
422	    tail_lines: 200
423	  router:
424	    timeout_s: 300
425	    max_turns: 25
426	
427	# ─── review-aggregator (leaf, ADVISORY) ──────────────────────────────────────
428	# C2 (#1141, ADR-040 §3/§4): merges the review_lenses members' results — the
429	# lens_result set the engine hands it (ADR-055 §1.4, #1842) — into ONE advisory
430	# merge-readiness report (review-report.json + review-report.md). Does NO LLM call
431	# — it merges lens JSON only. Bound by role review_aggregator to
432	# plugins/agent/review-aggregator. Requires lens_result: with no lens result the
433	# engine refuses it, and an empty set reports needs_attention, never "ready"
434	# (#1753). Never recommends a merge action, never blocks.
435	# The report.json filename is unchanged, so merge / pr-delivery consume it as before.
436	review-aggregator:
437	  gate: auto
438	  roles: [review_aggregator]
439	  io:
440	    destinations: [file, stdout]
441	    tail_lines: 200
442	
443	# ─── pr (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
444	# T0 tool stage (ADR-013): opens the pull request; no LLM call.
445	pr:
446	  gate: auto
447	  roles: [pr]
448	  io:
449	    destinations: [file, stdout]
450	    tail_lines: 200
451	
452	# ─── release (always-run, ADR-054 §7) ────────────────────────────────────────
453	# Frees live resources — process groups, locks, handles — and DELETES NOTHING,
454	# so a failed run keeps every byte of its evidence on disk. The teardown plugin
455	# pins its own scope to `release`; `purge` is operator-only and unreachable from
456	# any run path (`zbuild clean --purge`).
457	#
458	# timeout_s is 30 and is load-bearing, not a formality: this stage runs inside
459	# the EXIT trap, so a cleanup hook that blocks would turn Ctrl-C into a hang —
460	# the exact class of bug the mechanism exists to prevent.
461	release:
462	  gate: auto
463	  roles: [teardown]
464	  router:
465	    timeout_s: 30
466	  io:
467	    destinations: [file]
468	    tail_lines: 50
469	
470	# ─── persist (always-run, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ───────────────────────────
471	# Snapshots the artifact area to zbuild/state/issue-<N> and PUSHES it, on every
472	# exit path. Runs AFTER release, and that order is load-bearing: release frees
473	# live resources and must stay fast, while this does network I/O and can block
474	# on auth or a dead remote. Persist last means a bad network can never delay an
475	# abort.
476	#
477	# timeout_s is 120, four times release's 30. A push crosses the network; a
478	# process-group kill does not.
479	persist:
480	  gate: auto
481	  roles: [persist]
482	  router:
483	    timeout_s: 120
484	  io:
485	    destinations: [file]
486	    tail_lines: 50
487	
488	# ─── hydrate (first in flow, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ────────────────────────
489	# Pulls prior artifacts for this issue out of zbuild/state/issue-<N> so each
490	# stage's prior-output seam can seed from earlier work. Runs BEFORE intake, and
491	# is NOT always-run — there is nothing to hydrate at the end of a run.
492	#
493	# It fetches origin's copy first, which is what makes a fresh CI clone able to
494	# restore at all; a LOCAL snapshot still wins on read, because it may carry work
495	# an earlier push never delivered.
496	hydrate:
497	  gate: auto
498	  roles: [hydrate]
499	  router:
500	    timeout_s: 60
501	  io:
502	    destinations: [file]
503	    tail_lines: 50
504

file.content:
id: simple
name: Simple Pipeline
extends: null

# ADR-037 §4: per-template merge policy. Wired to runtime behavior in #975.
merge_policy: auto_unless_flagged

defaults:
  strategy: map

# ─── Flow ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Simplified pipeline (ADR-037 EPIC #966 / ADR-040 EPIC #1129): 7 top-level flow
# units — intake, plan, design, build_test_cycle, review_lenses, review-aggregator,
# pr — where build_test_cycle groups the build/test leaves plus the decomposed
# mechanical gate stages, and review_lenses is the advisory lens group.
#
# I10-A..C historically wrapped build/test/objective-gate in build_test_cycle.
# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 — amends ADR-013/ADR-021/ADR-019; executes ADR-037 §6) CUT
# OVER convergence from the retired monolithic objective-gate to the composable
# mechanical gates + gate-aggregator; the objective-gate plugin was then removed
# in B7 (#1139). The single merge-blocking construct is the gate-aggregator
# verdict (ADR-040 §5), reached via the cycle's exit_when.
#
# C3 (#1142, ADR-040 §3 — supersedes ADR-038's single-stage fan-out; ADR-039
# parallel group; follows ADR-030 scope governance) CUTS OVER the lens side: the
# monolithic `review` stage (ADR-038's hand-rolled review-report fan-out, now
# UNREFERENCED here) is replaced by `review_lenses` — a `type: map over: lenses`
# `aggregate: advisory` group (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2; was `type: parallel`) —
# one work unit per lens element — followed by
# `review-aggregator`, which merges the per-lens results into ONE advisory
# merge-readiness report. The lens group is ADVISORY: it NEVER feeds the cycle's
# exit_when/convergence (that remains the gate-aggregator, ADR-040 §5) and never
# blocks merge. The B5 no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
flow:
  - hydrate
  - intake
  - plan
  - delivery_loop
  - review_lenses
  - review-aggregator
  - pr

# ─── always_run (#1831) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Stages that run on EVERY exit path — success, non-zero rc, SIGINT, SIGTERM,
# timeout — in the order listed, after the flow has ended.
#
# This replaces a hardcoded dispatch in the runner's EXIT trap, which named one
# plugin by DIRECTORY (`plugins/tool/teardown`) and degraded silently to a no-op
# if it was absent. "Runs on every exit path" is a property of the FLOW, so it
# belongs in the template that defines the flow — not at a line number inside a
# 3000-line runner, where an edit can drop it without anything noticing. #1878
# found exactly that failure in the sibling mechanism: the snapshot was never
# called.
#
# An always-run stage is NOT part of `flow:` and never enters the flow's stage
# list: it has no place in the pipeline's data dependencies and must not affect
# convergence, verdicts, or the run's exit status.
#
# Each entry is an ordinary top-level stage section — resolved by `roles:` like
# any other stage, and bounded by its own `router.timeout_s`. A name here with
# no section, or a section with no `roles:`, REFUSES the template rather than
# quietly running nothing.
always_run:
  - release
  - persist

# ─── delivery_loop (cycle) — #2271, ADR-068 ─────────────────────────────────
# One outer loop holds the design loop and the build loop. Every stage sees
# every finding and says in its own result what it did about each; the engine
# never decides who owns a finding, and nothing jumps backwards.
#   - A design loop that runs out of rounds ends this round (build is skipped)
#     and this loop goes round. When this loop's rounds are spent, the run stops.
delivery_loop:
  type: cycle
  description: Design, then build, until both pass — going round when a finding needs design
  flow:
    - design_verify_cycle
    - build_test_cycle
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: design_verify_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: build_test_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: halt

# ─── design_verify_cycle (cycle) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-046 (#1218, EPIC #1216): give the design stage an independent verifier that
# loops back TO it BEFORE the build cycle — so design/contract defects are caught
# where they are authored, not deep in the build cycle. Modelled on standard.yaml's
# design_impact_cycle (standard.yaml:40-67), which simple.yaml historically lacked.
#
# Members: design → design-gate. design-gate is a T0 tool (ADR-037 §3): a pure-grep
# PRE-build structural gate over design.md + the red-first stubs design writes. It
# is BOTH a cycle member AND convergence:gate, so the typed-aggregator preflight
# rule (A) is satisfied by binding exit_when directly to it — a single gate, no
# separate aggregator needed (contrast build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator, which
# rolls up MANY gates). exit_when fires on design-gate.verdict == pass.
# max_iterations: 2, on_max: halt (#2176): a contract the gate still rejects is
# not built. Nested in delivery_loop (#2271), running out of rounds ends that
# loop's round — build is skipped — and the outer loop goes round.
#
# Feedback: design.design → design.prior_design (self-edge) — mirrors
# design_impact_cycle so iter N+1 refines rather than re-creates (#773 lesson).
#
design_verify_cycle:
  type: cycle
  description: Verify the design contract is build-ready until design-gate passes
  flow:
    - design
    # #1683: does the design cover what the ISSUE asked for? Design is the only
    # reader of the issue, so nothing else confirms the SPECs are a faithful
    # statement of the ask. Inside the cycle, so a finding reaches design itself
    # on the next iteration.
    - spec-coverage
    - design-gate
  # #1284/ADR-047 multi-condition: BOTH must hold. spec-coverage may gate under
  # ADR-040 §5 as amended by #2040 — the standard it judges against is the
  # ISSUE, which design cannot re-author, so the only way to converge is to
  # actually cover it.
  #
  # `ne uncovered` rather than `eq covered`: `unreadable` must not stall the
  # cycle. intake writes a placeholder when the issue fetch fails (#1804), and
  # failing closed there would break every offline run for a condition that is
  # not design's fault. The finding still ships in the summary.
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: design-gate, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: spec-coverage, field: verdict, op: ne, value: uncovered }
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: halt
  feedback:
    - from:
        stage: design
        output: design
      to:
        stage: design
        input: design
        required: false

# ─── spec-coverage (leaf, gate) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Model-judged but admissible on the convergence path (ADR-040 §5 / #2040): its
# standard is the issue, produced by intake OUTSIDE this cycle, so the judged
# party cannot re-author it.
spec-coverage:
  gate: auto
  roles: [spec_coverage]
  # A product owner asks "was what was asked for delivered?" — intent-seeking,
  # which is wrong for judging an assertion against a SPEC (the bug there
  # survives charity) and exactly right here, where the question IS about intent.
  persona: product-owner
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── test-author (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not sit on the convergence path.
# Its work is verified mechanically downstream — the test stage runs the
# assertions and acceptance-gate proves they discriminate.
test-author:
  gate: auto
  roles: [test_author]
  # #2188: no authored assertions → the cycle stops before build. Otherwise build
  # writes its own tests, the defect #2022 exists to prevent (#1849 run
  # 35949629759). Its failure is retried first (the stage's `retry:` budget).
  blocking: true
  router:
    # #2188: the same budget as build — authoring a 15–25 SPEC contract is
    # build-sized work (#1849: two 600s calls both timed out mid-write).
    # #2225: per CALL now — test-author loops until it says it is done, like
    # build, so a big contract takes more calls instead of overrunning one.
    # At most 4 calls: timeouts that are not back-to-back let the loop go on,
    # so the ceiling is calls × timeout — 60 min here (review #2229).
    timeout_s: 900
    max_turns: 0
    max_iterations: 4

# ─── spec-correspondence (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not gate. Its finding reaches
# test-author on the next iteration through the summary channel.
spec-correspondence:
  gate: auto
  roles: [spec_correspondence]
  # #1627: personas were consumed only by review lenses and NO template carried
  # a persona: key, so a persona manifest resolved to nothing. This is the first
  # stage-level binding. QA assures traceability; it does not test — which is
  # what separates it from test-strategist, whose instinct shown a mismatched
  # assertion is to repair it and answer yes.
  persona: quality-assurance
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── assertion-integrity (leaf, gate) ────────────────────────────────────────
# Mechanical, no model.route — so it MAY gate (ADR-040 §5).
assertion-integrity:
  gate: auto
  roles: [assertion_integrity]

# ─── issue-acceptance (leaf, gate) ───────────────────────────────────────────
# #1849: the finished change against the ISSUE. A model call on the convergence
# path is allowed for the same reason as spec-coverage (ADR-040 §5 as amended by
# #2040): its standard is the issue, which the judged stages cannot re-author.
issue-acceptance:
  gate: auto
  roles: [issue_acceptance]
  # Same question spec-coverage asks of the design — "was what was asked for
  # delivered?" — now asked of the code.
  persona: product-owner
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── build_test_cycle (cycle) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 §2/§5): the cycle re-runs build/test then the decomposed
# mechanical gates (shape-floor, acceptance-gate, secret-scan) and finally the
# gate-aggregator, which collapses every must-pass gate into ONE convergence
# verdict. exit_when fires on gate-aggregator.verdict == pass — the ADR-019
# fail-closed contract re-expressed as a single composable construct (ADR-040 §5).
# (#1129 Change C, ADR-012: the lint/coverage/mutation read-out gates were
# DROPPED as cycle members — they were redundant. mutation and lint both run in
# the test suite (run-tests.sh --tier all / npm test, which the `test` cycle
# member runs), so a lint or mutation regression fails the `test` gate directly.
# coverage is NOT folded into the suite — it stays enforced by the dedicated CI
# `coverage` job (re-running it inside --tier all would trip the #983 re-entrancy
# guard; see ADR-012 "Coverage gating"). The lint-gate/coverage-gate/mutation-gate
# plugins remain canonical (ADR-013) but dormant for future reuse.)
# The individual gates are NON-blocking (no blocking:true):
# they emit verdict-in-artifact (ADR-004) and the cycle iterates-to-fix; the loop
# converges via exit_when, never via per-gate hard-blocks. max_iterations: 3.
# Nested in delivery_loop (#2271): running out of rounds hands back to that loop,
# which goes round from design.
build_test_cycle:
  type: cycle
  description: Build, test, and run the mechanical gates until gate-aggregator passes
  flow:
    # #2022: test-author runs FIRST. It authors the acceptance assertions from
    # the design's SPEC sentences before build implements against them, so the
    # code and the assertion are two independent readings rather than two
    # artifacts of one. It never sees the diff.
    - test-author
    # #2034: judges whether each assertion tests what its SPEC SAYS — the one
    # link execution cannot reach (a passing test proves the implementation
    # satisfies the ASSERTION, never that the assertion satisfies the SENTENCE).
    # Before build, because its question needs the requirement and the assertion
    # and not the implementation — which at this point does not exist yet, so
    # its isolation is a fact of placement rather than a rule to enforce.
    - spec-correspondence
    - build
    - test
    - shape-floor
    - acceptance-gate
    - secret-scan
    # #2022: mechanical backstop. The spawn denies build Edit() on the declared
    # TESTFILES, but #1919 P5 measured that a Write(...) deny rule matches
    # nothing — prevention is incomplete by construction. A fail here makes the
    # aggregate non-pass, so the cycle iterates rather than converging on a
    # rewritten assertion.
    - assertion-integrity
    # #1849: the finished change judged against the ISSUE, not the SPECs — the
    # only check after spec-coverage that reads the issue at all. A convergence
    # gate, so gate-aggregator's roster makes it must-pass; each unmet
    # requirement is a numbered finding.
    - issue-acceptance
    - gate-aggregator
  exit_when:
    stage: gate-aggregator
    field: verdict
    op: eq
    value: pass
  max_iterations: 3
  on_max: continue
  # The cycle CONVERGES rather than spinning build(no-op)→…→gate-aggregator(fail)
  # because the aggregator's consolidated gate-feedback.md reaches build. B2
  # (ADR-040): the gate-aggregator is the SINGLE collector of failure detail,
  # merging every failing mechanical gate into one document. It used to arrive
  # through a feedback: wire plus a bespoke reader; #1979 retired both — the
  # aggregator marks that output `summary: true` (#1976) and the engine injects
  # it, framed by verdict, with no per-consumer wiring.
# ─── intake (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
intake:
  gate: auto
  roles: [intake]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── plan (leaf) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
plan:
  gate: auto
  roles: [planner]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    # 45 (raised from the 25 default, #1442) — same starvation the impact stage
    # hit (#impact-max-turns): scope exploration needs headroom. The planner is
    # also told this budget in its prompt and biased to converge before it runs out.
    max_turns: 45

# ─── design (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ───────────────────────────────
design:
  gate: auto
  roles: [designer]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 600
    max_turns: 0

# ─── design-gate (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ──────────────────────────
# T0 tool gate (ADR-046, #1218): PRE-build mechanical structural gate. Pure grep
# over design.md (NO LLM, NO baseline — ADR-037 §3). Runs the 5 structural
# checks (scope non-empty; acceptance block well-formed; every SPEC has a status
# — [code], [no-code] or [done] with evidence that exists (ADR-069); every [code]
# SPEC declares a TESTFILE; WIRING present/none + paths exist) and reports ALL
# violations in ONE pass. verdict-in-artifact; the design_verify_cycle exit_when
# reads design-gate.verdict == pass. Bound by role design_gate.
design-gate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [design_gate]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── build (leaf, cycle member) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
build:
  gate: auto
  roles: [builder]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 900
    max_turns: 0

# ─── test (leaf, cycle member) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
test:
  gate: auto
  roles: [tester]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── shape-floor (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1134): un-gameable shape-floor check. verdict-in-artifact.
shape-floor:
  gate: auto
  roles: [shape_floor]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── acceptance-gate (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
# Mechanical (non-LLM) acceptance-contract gate (ADR-036, #922). No-op pass when
# the design acceptance block is absent (its design input is required:false in the
# manifest — design already emits the SPEC/WIRING block). Its gate_result feeds
# the acceptance→build feedback edge above.
# ADR-036 #1188: negctl_timeout_s bounds each SPEC negative-control / reachability
# test run (seconds). A timeout is classified INFRA (non-terminal), never a
# violation. Override per-run with ZBUILD_NEGCTL_TIMEOUT (env wins).
acceptance-gate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [acceptance_gate]
  negctl_timeout_s: 60
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 600
    max_turns: 10

# ─── secret-scan (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1136): blocks hardcoded secrets/.env in the diff.
# verdict-in-artifact (skip on empty diff).
secret-scan:
  gate: auto
  roles: [secret_scan]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── gate-aggregator (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
# T0 convergence aggregator (ADR-040 §2/§5, #1137): collapses the must-pass gate
# set into ONE verdict. This is the cycle's exit_when source and the single
# merge-blocking construct in the decomposed pipeline. verdict-in-artifact.
gate-aggregator:
  gate: auto
  roles: [gate_aggregator]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── review_lenses (map group, ADVISORY) ─────────────────────────────────────
# issue #1295 (ADR-047 §2): converted from `type: parallel` to `type: map`.
# Each element (security, performance, red-team, correctness, scope) becomes one
# work unit dispatched to the review-lens plugin (provides.role: review_lens).
# `as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID` maps each element into the env var the review-lens
# plugin already reads to derive the lens identity — so the plugin is unchanged
# from its per-stage form. This eliminates the five separate lens-* stage
# definitions while preserving the same five isolated LLM calls and the same
# lens-<element>.json artifact names (ADR-038 §2 isolated-call discipline).
#
# aggregate: advisory — this group is NEVER on a merge-blocking path (ADR-040 §4).
# Convergence is owned by the build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator exit_when above;
# the B5 (#1137) no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
review_lenses:
  type: map
  over: lenses
  elements:
    - security
    - performance
    - red-team
    - correctness
    - scope
    - sre
  roles: [review_lens]
  as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID
  max_parallel: 4
  on_member_error: continue
  aggregate: advisory
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    max_turns: 25

# ─── review-aggregator (leaf, ADVISORY) ──────────────────────────────────────
# C2 (#1141, ADR-040 §3/§4): merges the review_lenses members' results — the
# lens_result set the engine hands it (ADR-055 §1.4, #1842) — into ONE advisory
# merge-readiness report (review-report.json + review-report.md). Does NO LLM call
# — it merges lens JSON only. Bound by role review_aggregator to
# plugins/agent/review-aggregator. Requires lens_result: with no lens result the
# engine refuses it, and an empty set reports needs_attention, never "ready"
# (#1753). Never recommends a merge action, never blocks.
# The report.json filename is unchanged, so merge / pr-delivery consume it as before.
review-aggregator:
  gate: auto
  roles: [review_aggregator]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── pr (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool stage (ADR-013): opens the pull request; no LLM call.
pr:
  gate: auto
  roles: [pr]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── release (always-run, ADR-054 §7) ────────────────────────────────────────
# Frees live resources — process groups, locks, handles — and DELETES NOTHING,
# so a failed run keeps every byte of its evidence on disk. The teardown plugin
# pins its own scope to `release`; `purge` is operator-only and unreachable from
# any run path (`zbuild clean --purge`).
#
# timeout_s is 30 and is load-bearing, not a formality: this stage runs inside
# the EXIT trap, so a cleanup hook that blocks would turn Ctrl-C into a hang —
# the exact class of bug the mechanism exists to prevent.
release:
  gate: auto
  roles: [teardown]
  router:
    timeout_s: 30
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# ─── persist (always-run, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ───────────────────────────
# Snapshots the artifact area to zbuild/state/issue-<N> and PUSHES it, on every
# exit path. Runs AFTER release, and that order is load-bearing: release frees
# live resources and must stay fast, while this does network I/O and can block
# on auth or a dead remote. Persist last means a bad network can never delay an
# abort.
#
# timeout_s is 120, four times release's 30. A push crosses the network; a
# process-group kill does not.
persist:
  gate: auto
  roles: [persist]
  router:
    timeout_s: 120
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# ─── hydrate (first in flow, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ────────────────────────
# Pulls prior artifacts for this issue out of zbuild/state/issue-<N> so each
# stage's prior-output seam can seed from earlier work. Runs BEFORE intake, and
# is NOT always-run — there is nothing to hydrate at the end of a run.
#
# It fetches origin's copy first, which is what makes a fresh CI clone able to
# restore at all; a LOCAL snapshot still wins on read, because it may carry work
# an earlier push never delivered.
hydrate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [hydrate]
  router:
    timeout_s: 60
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# [#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run reads stage_timeout_s (not
# router.timeout_s) for its time limit; simple.yaml carries stage_timeout_s
# for all stages at required values; router.timeout_s remains absent from the
# two always_run stages.
#
# [#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run kills through zbuild_pg_kill;
# no hand-rolled TERM/KILL sequence remains for stage dispatch.
#
# These tests FAIL on pre-change code (where _runner_dispatch_always_run reads
# _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_* and uses a hand-rolled kill sequence) and PASS
# after the change.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-6] always_run uses stage_timeout_s; [#1801/SPEC-10] zbuild_pg_kill"
setup_test_env "stage-timeout-always-run"

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-6] runner.sh reads _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_*, not _ROUTER_TIMEOUT ─
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run reads _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_*"

_runner="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# Extract the _runner_dispatch_always_run function body.
_ar_body=""
_ar_body="$(awk '/_runner_dispatch_always_run\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^    \}$/{exit}' "$_runner" 2>/dev/null || true)"

if [[ -z "$_ar_body" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run is defined in runner.sh" \
        "function body not found"
else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run is defined in runner.sh"

    # After the change: reads _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_*, not _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_*
    if grep -q '_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_' <<< "$_ar_body"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run reads _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_*"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run reads _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_*" \
            "_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_* not found — still using old _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_* or ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT"
    fi

    # The OLD variable must not be the primary source.
    # It may still exist as a fallback to ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S, but
    # _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_* must NOT be the limit variable the function uses.
    if grep -q '_ar_to.*_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT\|_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT.*_ar_to' <<< "$_ar_body"; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run no longer uses _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_* as its time limit" \
            "still reads _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_* for _ar_to — must use _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_* instead"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run no longer uses _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_* as its time limit"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml carries stage_timeout_s for all stages ────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml stage_timeout_s values"

_simple="$REPO_ROOT/config/templates/simple.yaml"
if [[ ! -f "$_simple" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] config/templates/simple.yaml exists" "not found"
else
    # Verify required stage_timeout_s values by parsing the template.
    # Each check verifies that the section contains `stage_timeout_s: N`.
    # Strategy: for each stage, confirm that stage_timeout_s appears in simple.yaml
    # with the required value by extracting the section and checking.
    _check_stage_timeout() {
        local _stage="$1" _expected_s="$2"
        # Find the stage section and look for stage_timeout_s: N within it.
        # Use awk to extract from the stage heading to the next top-level entry.
        local _found
        _found="$(awk -v stage="$_stage:" '
            $0 == stage { in_stage=1; next }
            in_stage && /^[a-zA-Z_]/ { exit }
            in_stage && /stage_timeout_s:/ { print; exit }
        ' "$_simple" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+')"

        if [[ "$_found" == "$_expected_s" ]]; then
            assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml $_stage: stage_timeout_s == ${_expected_s}s"
        else
            assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml $_stage: stage_timeout_s == ${_expected_s}s" \
                "got '${_found:-<absent>}'"
        fi
    }

    _check_stage_timeout "release" "30"
    _check_stage_timeout "persist" "120"
    _check_stage_timeout "test" "5400"
    _check_stage_timeout "build" "4200"
    _check_stage_timeout "design" "3900"
    _check_stage_timeout "plan" "1200"
    _check_stage_timeout "test-author" "900"
    _check_stage_timeout "spec-coverage" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "acceptance-gate" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "issue-acceptance" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "spec-correspondence" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "review_lenses" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "intake" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "pr" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "hydrate" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "secret-scan" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "shape-floor" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "design-gate" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "gate-aggregator" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "assertion-integrity" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "review-aggregator" "600"

    # ─── [#1801/SPEC-6] release and persist have no router.timeout_s ──────────
    # The two always_run stages convert their router.timeout_s to stage_timeout_s.
    # After the change they must not declare router.timeout_s.
    for _ar_stage in release persist; do
        _router_to=""
        _router_to="$(awk -v stage="$_ar_stage:" '
            $0 == stage { in_stage=1; next }
            in_stage && /^[a-zA-Z_]/ { exit }
            in_stage && /router:/ { in_router=1; next }
            in_stage && in_router && /timeout_s:/ { print; exit }
            in_stage && in_router && /^[[:space:]]+[a-z_]+:/ && !/timeout_s/ { in_router=0 }
        ' "$_simple" 2>/dev/null || true)"

        if [[ -n "$_router_to" ]]; then
            assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml $_ar_stage: no router.timeout_s (converted to stage_timeout_s)" \
                "router.timeout_s still present: $_router_to"
        else
            assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml $_ar_stage: no router.timeout_s (converted to stage_timeout_s)"
        fi
    done
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run uses zbuild_pg_kill ──────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run uses zbuild_pg_kill"

if [[ -n "$_ar_body" ]]; then
    if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill' <<< "$_ar_body"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run calls zbuild_pg_kill"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run calls zbuild_pg_kill" \
            "zbuild_pg_kill not found in function body"
    fi

    # The hand-rolled `kill -TERM -- -` pattern must be gone from this function.
    # (The pattern is `kill -TERM -- -"$_ar_pid"` in the old code.)
    if grep -qE 'kill -TERM -- -"\$_ar_pid"' <<< "$_ar_body"; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL sequence" \
            "found 'kill -TERM -- -\"\$_ar_pid\"' — replace with zbuild_pg_kill"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL sequence"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-10] lifecycle.sh uses zbuild_pg_kill for stage dispatch ──────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-10] lifecycle.sh uses zbuild_pg_kill (not hand-rolled TERM/KILL) for dispatch"

_lc="$REPO_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_lc" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh exists" "not found"
else
    if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill' "$_lc"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] lifecycle.sh calls zbuild_pg_kill for stage dispatch"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] lifecycle.sh calls zbuild_pg_kill for stage dispatch" \
            "zbuild_pg_kill not found — the per-dispatch watchdog must use it"
    fi
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# [#1801/SPEC-2] Killing a hung run hook stops the entire process group — a
# child ignoring TERM leaves no process alive after TERM + 10 s grace.
#
# The per-dispatch watchdog must:
#   1. Run the hook subshell under set -m (job-control mode) so the subshell
#      becomes a process-group leader.
#   2. Kill via zbuild_pg_kill, which sends TERM to the whole group and then
#      KILL after a grace period.
#   3. The grace period must be at least 10 s (so a hook that traps TERM has
#      enough time to flush, but a child ignoring TERM is killed).
#
# These tests use source-level checks — the behavioral guarantee (no process
# survives) is enforced by SPEC-6b in the integration test. These FAIL on
# pre-change code (where lifecycle.sh has no watchdog at all) and PASS after.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-2] hung run hook kills entire process group (TERM + 10 s grace + KILL)"

_lc="$REPO_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh"

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call arms the hook under set -m ──────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call runs the hook under set -m (creates a process group)"

_phc_body=""
if [[ -f "$_lc" ]]; then
    _phc_body="$(awk '/^plugin_hook_call\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^\}$/{exit}' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi

if [[ -z "$_phc_body" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call is defined in lifecycle.sh" "not found"
else
    # set -m inside the function creates a new process group for the backgrounded subshell
    if grep -q 'set -m' <<< "$_phc_body"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call uses set -m to give the hook its own process group"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call uses set -m to give the hook its own process group" \
            "'set -m' not found in plugin_hook_call — the hook's group cannot be signalled"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-2] the kill goes through zbuild_pg_kill (group-scope) ────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-2] the timeout kill uses zbuild_pg_kill (group scope, not single-PID)"

if [[ -n "$_phc_body" ]]; then
    if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill' <<< "$_phc_body"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call uses zbuild_pg_kill (sends signal to whole group)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call uses zbuild_pg_kill (sends signal to whole group)" \
            "zbuild_pg_kill not found — a single-PID kill cannot reach descendants that ignore TERM"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-2] zbuild_pg_kill uses TERM + grace + KILL ──────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-2] zbuild_pg_kill uses TERM then KILL after grace (proc-group.sh)"

_pg="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_pg" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] scripts/lib/proc-group.sh exists" "not found"
else
    # zbuild_pg_kill must delegate to _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill, which does
    # TERM → poll → KILL.
    if grep -q '_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill' "$_pg"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] zbuild_pg_kill uses TERM+grace+KILL sequence (_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] zbuild_pg_kill uses TERM+grace+KILL sequence (_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill)" \
            "_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill not found in proc-group.sh"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-2] the grace is at least 10 s ───────────────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-2] the watchdog grace period is at least 10 s"

# The design specifies TERM + 10 s grace + KILL. Verify that the watchdog in
# lifecycle.sh passes a grace of >= 10 to zbuild_pg_kill or that the default
# grace in _zbuild_pg_grace is sufficiently large.
# Check that the value 10 (or larger) appears in the context of zbuild_pg_kill
# invocations in lifecycle.sh.
if [[ -n "$_phc_body" ]]; then
    # Look for zbuild_pg_kill called with a numeric grace >= 10.
    # Accept the pattern: zbuild_pg_kill "$var" 10 or zbuild_pg_kill "$pid" "$grace"
    # where the literal in the source is >= 10.
    _grace_ok=0
    if grep -qE 'zbuild_pg_kill.*[[:space:]][0-9]+' <<< "$_phc_body"; then
        # Extract all numeric values following zbuild_pg_kill
        while IFS= read -r _val; do
            [[ "$_val" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$_val" -ge 10 ]] && { _grace_ok=1; break; }
        done < <(grep -oE 'zbuild_pg_kill[^)]*' <<< "$_phc_body" | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || true)
    fi
    # Also accept if the grace is passed via a variable (the design uses a configurable grace)
    if grep -qE 'zbuild_pg_kill[^)]*\$\{?[A-Za-z_]' <<< "$_phc_body"; then
        _grace_ok=1
    fi

    if [[ "$_grace_ok" -eq 1 ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] watchdog grace period is >= 10 s (or variable-derived)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] watchdog grace period is >= 10 s (or variable-derived)" \
            "no zbuild_pg_kill call with grace >= 10 found in plugin_hook_call"
    fi
fi

print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

# Scrub ALL _TPL_STAGE_BLOCKING_<id> exports at load-entry, unconditionally.
    # BL| rows are emitted only for stages that declare blocking:, so any stale export —
    # left by a prior load_template call, by a stage that is absent from this
    # template's flow entirely, OR inherited from the process environment on a
    # cold-start first load — would otherwise survive and mis-mark a non-blocking
    # stage as blocking (ADR-013, issue #952 follow-up to #863). Iterating over
    # the prior _TPL_STAGES was a no-op on the first load; prefix expansion over
    # the live environment closes that cold-start gap.
    local _stale_bl
    for _stale_bl in "${!_TPL_STAGE_BLOCKING_@}"; do
        # Defensive: only unset well-formed identifier names ([A-Za-z0-9_]+),
        # never a name assembled from unvalidated input.
        [[ "$_stale_bl" =~ ^_TPL_STAGE_BLOCKING_[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ ]] || continue
        unset "$_stale_bl"
    done

    _TPL_STAGES=()
    _TPL_ALWAYS_RUN=()
    _TPL_CYCLES=()
    _TPL_PARALLEL_GROUPS=()
    _TPL_MAP_GROUPS=()
    # ADR-027 (Wave 17-B #703): shape detector. The new shape uses `flow:` at
    # top level + per-stage top-level sections discriminated by `type:`. The
    # old shape (Wave 15-D era) uses `stages:` + `stage_definitions:`. Detect
    # which we're loading; old shape routes through the legacy parsers
    # unchanged AND fires `template.deprecated_shape` so operators can find
    # stragglers before the shim removal (one release window).
    local _tpl_shape="old"
    if _tpl_is_new_shape "$template_file"; then
        _tpl_shape="new"
    else
        # Emit the deprecation event with run_id cleared so it does not enter
        # any C6-style "last-event-for-this-run" precondition chain (template
        # load is a process-level concern, not a pipeline-run event). The
        # event still appears in events.jsonl for ops-dashboard visibility.
        (
            unset ZBUILD_RUN_ID
            eb_emit_event "template.deprecated_shape" \
                "template_file=$template_file" "shape=pre_adr_027" \
                2>/dev/null || true
        )
    fi

    # ADR-021 v2 parser: scan `stages:` block, emitting interleaved S|/IC|/FB|
    # rows. Inline cycle entries (IC|) reference cycle member stages by id;
    # per-stage attrs for those members come from `stage_definitions:` (parsed
    # separately below).
    # ADR-027 (Wave 17-B): new-shape templates are translated by
    # _tpl_translate_new_shape into the same pipe-delimited row format the
    # legacy pipeline downstream code already consumes — single internal
    # representation; the shim is purely upstream.
    local stage_rows defs_rows
    if [[ "$_tpl_shape" == "new" ]]; then
        local _translated; _translated="$(_tpl_translate_new_shape "$template_file")" || return 1
        stage_rows="${_translated%%$'\037'*}"
        defs_rows="${_translated#*$'\037'}"
    else
        stage_rows="$(_tpl_parse_stages_v2 "$template_file")"
        defs_rows="$(_tpl_parse_stage_definitions "$template_file")"
    fi

    # Build map: stage id → "S|<id>|<roles>|<strategy>|<io...>|<router...>"
    # First load defs into the map; then non-cycle stage rows from `stages:`
    # also feed the map (regular stages declare their own attrs inline).
    local -A stage_def_row=()
    local row sid rest
    while IFS= read -r row; do
        [[ -z "$row" ]] && continue
        sid="${row%%|*}"
        rest="${row#*|}"
        stage_def_row["$sid"]="$rest"
    done <<< "$defs_rows"

    # Phase 1: collect ids in execution order + extract cycle metadata.
    local -a collected_ids=()
    local -a collected_io_dests=()
    local -a collected_io_tail=()
    local -a collected_io_redact=()
    local -a collected_router_timeout=()
    local -a collected_router_max_turns=()

# ADR-015 v3 (#440): per-stage io.redact (empty/true/false; empty = default true).
# LLM kind ignores "false" (always redacts).
template_stage_io_redact() {
    local stage_id="$1"
    local safe_id="${stage_id//-/_}"
    local var="_TPL_STAGE_IO_REDACT_${safe_id}"
    echo "${!var:-}"
}

# ADR-017 (#455): per-stage router.timeout_s (empty when unset → caller default 300).

                [[ -z "$pid" ]] && continue
                _TPL_PARALLEL_GROUPS+=("$pid")

                printf -v "_TPL_PARALLEL_FLOW_${psafe}"   '%s' "$pmembers"
                printf -v "_TPL_PARALLEL_MAX_${psafe}"    '%s' "$pmax"
                printf -v "_TPL_PARALLEL_ON_ERR_${psafe}" '%s' "${ponerr:-continue}"
                printf -v "_TPL_PARALLEL_AGGREGATE_${psafe}" '%s' "$pagg"
                export "_TPL_PARALLEL_FLOW_${psafe}" "_TPL_PARALLEL_MAX_${psafe}" \

                    [[ -z "$pm" ]] && continue

                    # rejects cross-group overlap separately).

                    for _p_ex in "${collected_ids[@]}"; do

                printf -v "_TPL_MAP_ELEMENTS_${im_safe}"  '%s' "$im_elements"
                printf -v "_TPL_MAP_MAX_${im_safe}"        '%s' "$im_max"

                printf -v "_TPL_MAP_AGGREGATE_${im_safe}" '%s' "$im_agg"

                       "_TPL_MAP_MAX_${im_safe}" "_TPL_MAP_ON_ERR_${im_safe}" \
                       "_TPL_MAP_AGGREGATE_${im_safe}" "_TPL_MAP_AS_${im_safe}" \

                stage_data_rows+=("$im_gid|$im_roles|$im_strat|$im_iod|$im_iot|$im_ior|$im_rt|$im_rmt|$im_rmi|$im_rre")
                collected_ids+=("$im_gid")
                collected_io_dests+=("$im_iod")
                collected_io_tail+=("$im_iot")
                collected_io_redact+=("$im_ior")
                collected_router_timeout+=("$im_rt")

# #2271: a loop's stages are collected as each loop's definition arrives —
    # inner loops first — so a direct member between two inner loops (impact,
    # between the design and build loops) would land last. Put each top-level
    # loop's stages back in the order they run.
    _tpl_order_by_flow stage_data_rows

    # Populate per-stage state (flat _TPL_STAGES[] + per-id env vars).
    local stage_id roles strategy io_dests io_tail io_redact router_timeout router_max_turns router_max_iterations router_retries
    for row in "${stage_data_rows[@]}"; do
        IFS='|' read -r stage_id roles strategy io_dests io_tail io_redact router_timeout router_max_turns router_max_iterations router_retries <<< "$row"
        [[ -z "$stage_id" ]] && continue
        _TPL_STAGES+=("$stage_id")
        local safe_id="${stage_id//-/_}"
        printf -v "_TPL_STAGE_ROLES_${safe_id}" '%s' "$roles"
        printf -v "_TPL_STAGE_STRATEGY_${safe_id}" '%s' "$strategy"
        printf -v "_TPL_STAGE_IO_DESTS_${safe_id}" '%s' "$io_dests"
        printf -v "_TPL_STAGE_IO_TAIL_${safe_id}" '%s' "$io_tail"
        printf -v "_TPL_STAGE_IO_REDACT_${safe_id}" '%s' "$io_redact"
        printf -v "_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_${safe_id}" '%s' "$router_timeout"
        printf -v "_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS_${safe_id}" '%s' "$router_max_turns"
        printf -v "_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_MAX_ITERATIONS_${safe_id}" '%s' "$router_max_iterations"
        printf -v "_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_RETRIES_${safe_id}" '%s' "$router_retries"
        export "_TPL_STAGE_ROLES_${safe_id}" \
               "_TPL_STAGE_STRATEGY_${safe_id}" \
               "_TPL_STAGE_IO_DESTS_${safe_id}" \
               "_TPL_STAGE_IO_TAIL_${safe_id}" \
               "_TPL_STAGE_IO_REDACT_${safe_id}" \
               "_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_${safe_id}" \
               "_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS_${safe_id}" \
               "_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_MAX_ITERATIONS_${safe_id}" \
               "_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_RETRIES_${safe_id}"
    done

    # ── #1831: always-run stages ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Parsed from the FILE, not from either shape's row stream, because
    # `always_run:` is a top-level key in BOTH shapes and its members are
    # top-level sections in both. Routing it through the new-shape translator —
    # which is what the first cut of this did — silently dropped it for every
    # old-shape template, and the parity fixture (old shape, `extends: simple`)
    # lost its teardown entirely. The golden caught it; nothing else would have.
    #
    # These stages are NOT in _TPL_STAGES[] and must never be: they have no
    # place in the flow's data dependencies and must not affect convergence,
    # verdicts, or the run's exit status.
    #
    # Fail CLOSED on a member with no section. An always-run stage that silently
    # does not exist is the failure this attribute was built to remove (#1878 —
    # "the snapshot was never called"), so a typo must refuse the template
    # rather than degrade to running nothing.
    local _ar_line _ar_id _ar_roles _ar_to _ar_safe
    while IFS='|' read -r _ar_id _ar_roles _ar_to; do
        [[ -z "$_ar_id" ]] && continue
        if [[ "$_ar_roles" == "__MISSING__" ]]; then
            error "load_template: always_run names '$_ar_id' but no top-level section defines it"
            return 1
        fi
        if [[ -z "$_ar_roles" ]]; then
            error "load_template: always_run stage '$_ar_id' declares no roles: — the runner resolves it by role"
            return 1
        fi
        _TPL_ALWAYS_RUN+=("$_ar_id")
        _ar_safe="${_ar_id//-/_}"
        printf -v "_TPL_STAGE_ROLES_${_ar_safe}"          '%s' "$_ar_roles"
        printf -v "_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_${_ar_safe}" '%s' "$_ar_to"
        export "_TPL_STAGE_ROLES_${_ar_safe}" "_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_${_ar_safe}"
    done < <(_tpl_parse_always_run "$template_file")

    _tpl_validate_cycles || return 1
    _tpl_validate_parallel || return 1
    _tpl_build_dispatch_units || return 1

    # ADR-027 (Wave 17-B #703): stage-type discriminator. Every stage in
    # _TPL_STAGES[] is `leaf` by default; cycle ids get `cycle`. The
    # orchestrator reads `_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_<id>` at dispatch time to decide
    # whether to recurse (cycle-as-member) or invoke the leaf path.
    local _st_id _st_safe
    for _st_id in "${_TPL_STAGES[@]}"; do
        _st_safe="${_st_id//-/_}"
        # Default: leaf. Cycle ids are overwritten below.
        printf -v "_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_${_st_safe}" '%s' "leaf"
        export "_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_${_st_safe}"
    done
    for _st_id in "${_TPL_CYCLES[@]}"; do
        _st_safe="${_st_id//-/_}"
        printf -v "_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_${_st_safe}" '%s' "cycle"
        export "_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_${_st_safe}"
        # ADR-027 lexicon parity: _TPL_CYCLE_FLOW_<id> aliases the existing
        # _TPL_CYCLE_STAGES_<id> so callers using ADR-027 names work.
        local _cf_src="_TPL_CYCLE_STAGES_${_st_safe}"
        printf -v "_TPL_CYCLE_FLOW_${_st_safe}" '%s' "${!_cf_src:-}"
        export "_TPL_CYCLE_FLOW_${_st_safe}"
    done
    # ADR-039 (#1130): parallel group ids get _TPL_STAGE_TYPE_<gid>=parallel
    # (sibling of the cycle discriminator). Members remain leaf (set above).
    for _st_id in "${_TPL_PARALLEL_GROUPS[@]}"; do
        _st_safe="${_st_id//-/_}"
        printf -v "_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_${_st_safe}" '%s' "parallel"
        export "_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_${_st_safe}"
    done
    # issue #1295 (ADR-047 §2): map group ids get _TPL_STAGE_TYPE_<gid>=map.
    # The group id itself is in _TPL_STAGES (set above to leaf); overwrite here.
    for _st_id in "${_TPL_MAP_GROUPS[@]}"; do
        _st_safe="${_st_id//-/_}"
        printf -v "_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_${_st_safe}" '%s' "map"
        export "_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_${_st_safe}"
    done

    # ADR-027 contract validator (Wave 17-B #703): reference-graph acyclicity.
    # If any cycle's flow transitively includes itself, refuse to load.
    _tpl_validate_flow_acyclic || return 1
}
