tool_use_result.originalFile:
id: simple
name: Simple Pipeline
extends: null

# ADR-037 §4: per-template merge policy. Wired to runtime behavior in #975.
merge_policy: auto_unless_flagged

defaults:
  strategy: map

# ─── Flow ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Simplified pipeline (ADR-037 EPIC #966 / ADR-040 EPIC #1129): 7 top-level flow
# units — intake, plan, design, build_test_cycle, review_lenses, review-aggregator,
# pr — where build_test_cycle groups the build/test leaves plus the decomposed
# mechanical gate stages, and review_lenses is the advisory lens group.
#
# I10-A..C historically wrapped build/test/objective-gate in build_test_cycle.
# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 — amends ADR-013/ADR-021/ADR-019; executes ADR-037 §6) CUT
# OVER convergence from the retired monolithic objective-gate to the composable
# mechanical gates + gate-aggregator; the objective-gate plugin was then removed
# in B7 (#1139). The single merge-blocking construct is the gate-aggregator
# verdict (ADR-040 §5), reached via the cycle's exit_when.
#
# C3 (#1142, ADR-040 §3 — supersedes ADR-038's single-stage fan-out; ADR-039
# parallel group; follows ADR-030 scope governance) CUTS OVER the lens side: the
# monolithic `review` stage (ADR-038's hand-rolled review-report fan-out, now
# UNREFERENCED here) is replaced by `review_lenses` — a `type: map over: lenses`
# `aggregate: advisory` group (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2; was `type: parallel`) —
# one work unit per lens element — followed by
# `review-aggregator`, which merges the per-lens results into ONE advisory
# merge-readiness report. The lens group is ADVISORY: it NEVER feeds the cycle's
# exit_when/convergence (that remains the gate-aggregator, ADR-040 §5) and never
# blocks merge. The B5 no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
flow:
  - hydrate
  - intake
  - plan
  - delivery_loop
  - review_lenses
  - review-aggregator
  - pr

# ─── always_run (#1831) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Stages that run on EVERY exit path — success, non-zero rc, SIGINT, SIGTERM,
# timeout — in the order listed, after the flow has ended.
#
# This replaces a hardcoded dispatch in the runner's EXIT trap, which named one
# plugin by DIRECTORY (`plugins/tool/teardown`) and degraded silently to a no-op
# if it was absent. "Runs on every exit path" is a property of the FLOW, so it
# belongs in the template that defines the flow — not at a line number inside a
# 3000-line runner, where an edit can drop it without anything noticing. #1878
# found exactly that failure in the sibling mechanism: the snapshot was never
# called.
#
# An always-run stage is NOT part of `flow:` and never enters the flow's stage
# list: it has no place in the pipeline's data dependencies and must not affect
# convergence, verdicts, or the run's exit status.
#
# Each entry is an ordinary top-level stage section — resolved by `roles:` like
# any other stage, and bounded by its own `router.timeout_s`. A name here with
# no section, or a section with no `roles:`, REFUSES the template rather than
# quietly running nothing.
always_run:
  - release
  - persist

# ─── delivery_loop (cycle) — #2271, ADR-068 ─────────────────────────────────
# One outer loop holds the design loop and the build loop. Every stage sees
# every finding and says in its own result what it did about each; the engine
# never decides who owns a finding, and nothing jumps backwards.
#   - A design loop that runs out of rounds ends this round (build is skipped)
#     and this loop goes round. When this loop's rounds are spent, the run stops.
delivery_loop:
  type: cycle
  description: Design, then build, until both pass — going round when a finding needs design
  flow:
    - design_verify_cycle
    - build_test_cycle
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: design_verify_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: build_test_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: halt

# ─── design_verify_cycle (cycle) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-046 (#1218, EPIC #1216): give the design stage an independent verifier that
# loops back TO it BEFORE the build cycle — so design/contract defects are caught
# where they are authored, not deep in the build cycle. Modelled on standard.yaml's
# design_impact_cycle (standard.yaml:40-67), which simple.yaml historically lacked.
#
# Members: design → design-gate. design-gate is a T0 tool (ADR-037 §3): a pure-grep
# PRE-build structural gate over design.md + the red-first stubs design writes. It
# is BOTH a cycle member AND convergence:gate, so the typed-aggregator preflight
# rule (A) is satisfied by binding exit_when directly to it — a single gate, no
# separate aggregator needed (contrast build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator, which
# rolls up MANY gates). exit_when fires on design-gate.verdict == pass.
# max_iterations: 2, on_max: halt (#2176): a contract the gate still rejects is
# not built. Nested in delivery_loop (#2271), running out of rounds ends that
# loop's round — build is skipped — and the outer loop goes round.
#
# Feedback: design.design → design.prior_design (self-edge) — mirrors
# design_impact_cycle so iter N+1 refines rather than re-creates (#773 lesson).
#
design_verify_cycle:
  type: cycle
  description: Verify the design contract is build-ready until design-gate passes
  flow:
    - design
    # #1683: does the design cover what the ISSUE asked for? Design is the only
    # reader of the issue, so nothing else confirms the SPECs are a faithful
    # statement of the ask. Inside the cycle, so a finding reaches design itself
    # on the next iteration.
    - spec-coverage
    - design-gate
  # #1284/ADR-047 multi-condition: BOTH must hold. spec-coverage may gate under
  # ADR-040 §5 as amended by #2040 — the standard it judges against is the
  # ISSUE, which design cannot re-author, so the only way to converge is to
  # actually cover it.
  #
  # `ne uncovered` rather than `eq covered`: `unreadable` must not stall the
  # cycle. intake writes a placeholder when the issue fetch fails (#1804), and
  # failing closed there would break every offline run for a condition that is
  # not design's fault. The finding still ships in the summary.
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: design-gate, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: spec-coverage, field: verdict, op: ne, value: uncovered }
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: halt
  feedback:
    - from:
        stage: design
        output: design
      to:
        stage: design
        input: design
        required: false

# ─── spec-coverage (leaf, gate) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Model-judged but admissible on the convergence path (ADR-040 §5 / #2040): its
# standard is the issue, produced by intake OUTSIDE this cycle, so the judged
# party cannot re-author it.
spec-coverage:
  gate: auto
  roles: [spec_coverage]
  # A product owner asks "was what was asked for delivered?" — intent-seeking,
  # which is wrong for judging an assertion against a SPEC (the bug there
  # survives charity) and exactly right here, where the question IS about intent.
  persona: product-owner
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── test-author (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not sit on the convergence path.
# Its work is verified mechanically downstream — the test stage runs the
# assertions and acceptance-gate proves they discriminate.
test-author:
  gate: auto
  roles: [test_author]
  # #2188: no authored assertions → the cycle stops before build. Otherwise build
  # writes its own tests, the defect #2022 exists to prevent (#1849 run
  # 35949629759). Its failure is retried first (the stage's `retry:` budget).
  blocking: true
  stage_timeout_s: 900
  router:
    # #2188: the same budget as build — authoring a 15–25 SPEC contract is
    # build-sized work (#1849: two 600s calls both timed out mid-write).
    # #2225: per CALL now — test-author loops until it says it is done, like
    # build, so a big contract takes more calls instead of overrunning one.
    # At most 4 calls: timeouts that are not back-to-back let the loop go on,
    # so the ceiling is calls × timeout — 60 min here (review #2229).
    timeout_s: 900
    max_turns: 0
    max_iterations: 4

# ─── spec-correspondence (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not gate. Its finding reaches
# test-author on the next iteration through the summary channel.
spec-correspondence:
  gate: auto
  roles: [spec_correspondence]
  # #1627: personas were consumed only by review lenses and NO template carried
  # a persona: key, so a persona manifest resolved to nothing. This is the first
  # stage-level binding. QA assures traceability; it does not test — which is
  # what separates it from test-strategist, whose instinct shown a mismatched
  # assertion is to repair it and answer yes.
  persona: quality-assurance
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── assertion-integrity (leaf, gate) ────────────────────────────────────────
# Mechanical, no model.route — so it MAY gate (ADR-040 §5).
assertion-integrity:
  gate: auto
  roles: [assertion_integrity]
  stage_timeout_s: 600

# ─── issue-acceptance (leaf, gate) ───────────────────────────────────────────
# #1849: the finished change against the ISSUE. A model call on the convergence
# path is allowed for the same reason as spec-coverage (ADR-040 §5 as amended by
# #2040): its standard is the issue, which the judged stages cannot re-author.
issue-acceptance:
  gate: auto
  roles: [issue_acceptance]
  # Same question spec-coverage asks of the design — "was what was asked for
  # delivered?" — now asked of the code.
  persona: product-owner
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── build_test_cycle (cycle) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 §2/§5): the cycle re-runs build/test then the decomposed
# mechanical gates (shape-floor, acceptance-gate, secret-scan) and finally the
# gate-aggregator, which collapses every must-pass gate into ONE convergence
# verdict. exit_when fires on gate-aggregator.verdict == pass — the ADR-019
# fail-closed contract re-expressed as a single composable construct (ADR-040 §5).
# (#1129 Change C, ADR-012: the lint/coverage/mutation read-out gates were
# DROPPED as cycle members — they were redundant. mutation and lint both run in
# the test suite (run-tests.sh --tier all / npm test, which the `test` cycle
# member runs), so a lint or mutation regression fails the `test` gate directly.
# coverage is NOT folded into the suite — it stays enforced by the dedicated CI
# `coverage` job (re-running it inside --tier all would trip the #983 re-entrancy
# guard; see ADR-012 "Coverage gating"). The lint-gate/coverage-gate/mutation-gate
# plugins remain canonical (ADR-013) but dormant for future reuse.)
# The individual gates are NON-blocking (no blocking:true):
# they emit verdict-in-artifact (ADR-004) and the cycle iterates-to-fix; the loop
# converges via exit_when, never via per-gate hard-blocks. max_iterations: 3.
# Nested in delivery_loop (#2271): running out of rounds hands back to that loop,
# which goes round from design.
build_test_cycle:
  type: cycle
  description: Build, test, and run the mechanical gates until gate-aggregator passes
  flow:
    # #2022: test-author runs FIRST. It authors the acceptance assertions from
    # the design's SPEC sentences before build implements against them, so the
    # code and the assertion are two independent readings rather than two
    # artifacts of one. It never sees the diff.
    - test-author
    # #2034: judges whether each assertion tests what its SPEC SAYS — the one
    # link execution cannot reach (a passing test proves the implementation
    # satisfies the ASSERTION, never that the assertion satisfies the SENTENCE).
    # Before build, because its question needs the requirement and the assertion
    # and not the implementation — which at this point does not exist yet, so
    # its isolation is a fact of placement rather than a rule to enforce.
    - spec-correspondence
    - build
    - test
    - shape-floor
    - acceptance-gate
    - secret-scan
    # #2022: mechanical backstop. The spawn denies build Edit() on the declared
    # TESTFILES, but #1919 P5 measured that a Write(...) deny rule matches
    # nothing — prevention is incomplete by construction. A fail here makes the
    # aggregate non-pass, so the cycle iterates rather than converging on a
    # rewritten assertion.
    - assertion-integrity
    # #1849: the finished change judged against the ISSUE, not the SPECs — the
    # only check after spec-coverage that reads the issue at all. A convergence
    # gate, so gate-aggregator's roster makes it must-pass; each unmet
    # requirement is a numbered finding.
    - issue-acceptance
    - gate-aggregator
  exit_when:
    stage: gate-aggregator
    field: verdict
    op: eq
    value: pass
  max_iterations: 3
  on_max: continue
  # The cycle CONVERGES rather than spinning build(no-op)→…→gate-aggregator(fail)
  # because the aggregator's consolidated gate-feedback.md reaches build. B2
  # (ADR-040): the gate-aggregator is the SINGLE collector of failure detail,
  # merging every failing mechanical gate into one document. It used to arrive
  # through a feedback: wire plus a bespoke reader; #1979 retired both — the
  # aggregator marks that output `summary: true` (#1976) and the engine injects
  # it, framed by verdict, with no per-consumer wiring.
# ─── intake (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
intake:
  gate: auto
  roles: [intake]
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── plan (leaf) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
plan:
  gate: auto
  roles: [planner]
  stage_timeout_s: 1200
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    # 45 (raised from the 25 default, #1442) — same starvation the impact stage
    # hit (#impact-max-turns): scope exploration needs headroom. The planner is
    # also told this budget in its prompt and biased to converge before it runs out.
    max_turns: 45

# ─── design (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ───────────────────────────────
design:
  gate: auto
  roles: [designer]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 600
    max_turns: 0

# ─── design-gate (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ──────────────────────────
# T0 tool gate (ADR-046, #1218): PRE-build mechanical structural gate. Pure grep
# over design.md (NO LLM, NO baseline — ADR-037 §3). Runs the 5 structural
# checks (scope non-empty; acceptance block well-formed; every SPEC has a status
# — [code], [no-code] or [done] with evidence that exists (ADR-069); every [code]
# SPEC declares a TESTFILE; WIRING present/none + paths exist) and reports ALL
# violations in ONE pass. verdict-in-artifact; the design_verify_cycle exit_when
# reads design-gate.verdict == pass. Bound by role design_gate.
design-gate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [design_gate]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── build (leaf, cycle member) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
build:
  gate: auto
  roles: [builder]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 900
    max_turns: 0

# ─── test (leaf, cycle member) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
test:
  gate: auto
  roles: [tester]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── shape-floor (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1134): un-gameable shape-floor check. verdict-in-artifact.
shape-floor:
  gate: auto
  roles: [shape_floor]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── acceptance-gate (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
# Mechanical (non-LLM) acceptance-contract gate (ADR-036, #922). No-op pass when
# the design acceptance block is absent (its design input is required:false in the
# manifest — design already emits the SPEC/WIRING block). Its gate_result feeds
# the acceptance→build feedback edge above.
# ADR-036 #1188: negctl_timeout_s bounds each SPEC negative-control / reachability
# test run (seconds). A timeout is classified INFRA (non-terminal), never a
# violation. Override per-run with ZBUILD_NEGCTL_TIMEOUT (env wins).
acceptance-gate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [acceptance_gate]
  negctl_timeout_s: 60
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 600
    max_turns: 10

# ─── secret-scan (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1136): blocks hardcoded secrets/.env in the diff.
# verdict-in-artifact (skip on empty diff).
secret-scan:
  gate: auto
  roles: [secret_scan]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── gate-aggregator (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
# T0 convergence aggregator (ADR-040 §2/§5, #1137): collapses the must-pass gate
# set into ONE verdict. This is the cycle's exit_when source and the single
# merge-blocking construct in the decomposed pipeline. verdict-in-artifact.
gate-aggregator:
  gate: auto
  roles: [gate_aggregator]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── review_lenses (map group, ADVISORY) ─────────────────────────────────────
# issue #1295 (ADR-047 §2): converted from `type: parallel` to `type: map`.
# Each element (security, performance, red-team, correctness, scope) becomes one
# work unit dispatched to the review-lens plugin (provides.role: review_lens).
# `as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID` maps each element into the env var the review-lens
# plugin already reads to derive the lens identity — so the plugin is unchanged
# from its per-stage form. This eliminates the five separate lens-* stage
# definitions while preserving the same five isolated LLM calls and the same
# lens-<element>.json artifact names (ADR-038 §2 isolated-call discipline).
#
# aggregate: advisory — this group is NEVER on a merge-blocking path (ADR-040 §4).
# Convergence is owned by the build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator exit_when above;
# the B5 (#1137) no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
review_lenses:
  type: map
  over: lenses
  elements:
    - security
    - performance
    - red-team
    - correctness
    - scope
    - sre
  roles: [review_lens]
  as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID
  max_parallel: 4
  on_member_error: continue
  aggregate: advisory
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    max_turns: 25

# ─── review-aggregator (leaf, ADVISORY) ──────────────────────────────────────
# C2 (#1141, ADR-040 §3/§4): merges the review_lenses members' results — the
# lens_result set the engine hands it (ADR-055 §1.4, #1842) — into ONE advisory
# merge-readiness report (review-report.json + review-report.md). Does NO LLM call
# — it merges lens JSON only. Bound by role review_aggregator to
# plugins/agent/review-aggregator. Requires lens_result: with no lens result the
# engine refuses it, and an empty set reports needs_attention, never "ready"
# (#1753). Never recommends a merge action, never blocks.
# The report.json filename is unchanged, so merge / pr-delivery consume it as before.
review-aggregator:
  gate: auto
  roles: [review_aggregator]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── pr (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool stage (ADR-013): opens the pull request; no LLM call.
pr:
  gate: auto
  roles: [pr]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── release (always-run, ADR-054 §7) ────────────────────────────────────────
# Frees live resources — process groups, locks, handles — and DELETES NOTHING,
# so a failed run keeps every byte of its evidence on disk. The teardown plugin
# pins its own scope to `release`; `purge` is operator-only and unreachable from
# any run path (`zbuild clean --purge`).
#
# timeout_s is 30 and is load-bearing, not a formality: this stage runs inside
# the EXIT trap, so a cleanup hook that blocks would turn Ctrl-C into a hang —
# the exact class of bug the mechanism exists to prevent.
release:
  gate: auto
  roles: [teardown]
  stage_timeout_s: 30
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# ─── persist (always-run, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ───────────────────────────
# Snapshots the artifact area to zbuild/state/issue-<N> and PUSHES it, on every
# exit path. Runs AFTER release, and that order is load-bearing: release frees
# live resources and must stay fast, while this does network I/O and can block
# on auth or a dead remote. Persist last means a bad network can never delay an
# abort.
#
# timeout_s is 120, four times release's 30. A push crosses the network; a
# process-group kill does not.
persist:
  gate: auto
  roles: [persist]
  stage_timeout_s: 120
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# ─── hydrate (first in flow, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ────────────────────────
# Pulls prior artifacts for this issue out of zbuild/state/issue-<N> so each
# stage's prior-output seam can seed from earlier work. Runs BEFORE intake, and
# is NOT always-run — there is nothing to hydrate at the end of a run.
#
# It fetches origin's copy first, which is what makes a fresh CI clone able to
# restore at all; a LOCAL snapshot still wins on read, because it may carry work
# an earlier push never delivered.
hydrate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [hydrate]
  router:
    timeout_s: 60
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

id: simple
name: Simple Pipeline
extends: null

# ADR-037 §4: per-template merge policy. Wired to runtime behavior in #975.
merge_policy: auto_unless_flagged

defaults:
  strategy: map

# ─── Flow ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Simplified pipeline (ADR-037 EPIC #966 / ADR-040 EPIC #1129): 7 top-level flow
# units — intake, plan, design, build_test_cycle, review_lenses, review-aggregator,
# pr — where build_test_cycle groups the build/test leaves plus the decomposed
# mechanical gate stages, and review_lenses is the advisory lens group.
#
# I10-A..C historically wrapped build/test/objective-gate in build_test_cycle.
# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 — amends ADR-013/ADR-021/ADR-019; executes ADR-037 §6) CUT
# OVER convergence from the retired monolithic objective-gate to the composable
# mechanical gates + gate-aggregator; the objective-gate plugin was then removed
# in B7 (#1139). The single merge-blocking construct is the gate-aggregator
# verdict (ADR-040 §5), reached via the cycle's exit_when.
#
# C3 (#1142, ADR-040 §3 — supersedes ADR-038's single-stage fan-out; ADR-039
# parallel group; follows ADR-030 scope governance) CUTS OVER the lens side: the
# monolithic `review` stage (ADR-038's hand-rolled review-report fan-out, now
# UNREFERENCED here) is replaced by `review_lenses` — a `type: map over: lenses`
# `aggregate: advisory` group (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2; was `type: parallel`) —
# one work unit per lens element — followed by
# `review-aggregator`, which merges the per-lens results into ONE advisory
# merge-readiness report. The lens group is ADVISORY: it NEVER feeds the cycle's
# exit_when/convergence (that remains the gate-aggregator, ADR-040 §5) and never
# blocks merge. The B5 no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
flow:
  - hydrate
  - intake
  - plan
  - delivery_loop
  - review_lenses
  - review-aggregator
  - pr

# ─── always_run (#1831) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Stages that run on EVERY exit path — success, non-zero rc, SIGINT, SIGTERM,
# timeout — in the order listed, after the flow has ended.
#
# This replaces a hardcoded dispatch in the runner's EXIT trap, which named one
# plugin by DIRECTORY (`plugins/tool/teardown`) and degraded silently to a no-op
# if it was absent. "Runs on every exit path" is a property of the FLOW, so it
# belongs in the template that defines the flow — not at a line number inside a
# 3000-line runner, where an edit can drop it without anything noticing. #1878
# found exactly that failure in the sibling mechanism: the snapshot was never
# called.
#
# An always-run stage is NOT part of `flow:` and never enters the flow's stage
# list: it has no place in the pipeline's data dependencies and must not affect
# convergence, verdicts, or the run's exit status.
#
# Each entry is an ordinary top-level stage section — resolved by `roles:` like
# any other stage, and bounded by its own `router.timeout_s`. A name here with
# no section, or a section with no `roles:`, REFUSES the template rather than
# quietly running nothing.
always_run:
  - release
  - persist

# ─── delivery_loop (cycle) — #2271, ADR-068 ─────────────────────────────────
# One outer loop holds the design loop and the build loop. Every stage sees
# every finding and says in its own result what it did about each; the engine
# never decides who owns a finding, and nothing jumps backwards.
#   - A design loop that runs out of rounds ends this round (build is skipped)
#     and this loop goes round. When this loop's rounds are spent, the run stops.
delivery_loop:
  type: cycle
  description: Design, then build, until both pass — going round when a finding needs design
  flow:
    - design_verify_cycle
    - build_test_cycle
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: design_verify_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: build_test_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: halt

# ─── design_verify_cycle (cycle) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-046 (#1218, EPIC #1216): give the design stage an independent verifier that
# loops back TO it BEFORE the build cycle — so design/contract defects are caught
# where they are authored, not deep in the build cycle. Modelled on standard.yaml's
# design_impact_cycle (standard.yaml:40-67), which simple.yaml historically lacked.
#
# Members: design → design-gate. design-gate is a T0 tool (ADR-037 §3): a pure-grep
# PRE-build structural gate over design.md + the red-first stubs design writes. It
# is BOTH a cycle member AND convergence:gate, so the typed-aggregator preflight
# rule (A) is satisfied by binding exit_when directly to it — a single gate, no
# separate aggregator needed (contrast build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator, which
# rolls up MANY gates). exit_when fires on design-gate.verdict == pass.
# max_iterations: 2, on_max: halt (#2176): a contract the gate still rejects is
# not built. Nested in delivery_loop (#2271), running out of rounds ends that
# loop's round — build is skipped — and the outer loop goes round.
#
# Feedback: design.design → design.prior_design (self-edge) — mirrors
# design_impact_cycle so iter N+1 refines rather than re-creates (#773 lesson).
#
design_verify_cycle:
  type: cycle
  description: Verify the design contract is build-ready until design-gate passes
  flow:
    - design
    # #1683: does the design cover what the ISSUE asked for? Design is the only
    # reader of the issue, so nothing else confirms the SPECs are a faithful
    # statement of the ask. Inside the cycle, so a finding reaches design itself
    # on the next iteration.
    - spec-coverage
    - design-gate
  # #1284/ADR-047 multi-condition: BOTH must hold. spec-coverage may gate under
  # ADR-040 §5 as amended by #2040 — the standard it judges against is the
  # ISSUE, which design cannot re-author, so the only way to converge is to
  # actually cover it.
  #
  # `ne uncovered` rather than `eq covered`: `unreadable` must not stall the
  # cycle. intake writes a placeholder when the issue fetch fails (#1804), and
  # failing closed there would break every offline run for a condition that is
  # not design's fault. The finding still ships in the summary.
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: design-gate, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: spec-coverage, field: verdict, op: ne, value: uncovered }
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: halt
  feedback:
    - from:
        stage: design
        output: design
      to:
        stage: design
        input: design
        required: false

# ─── spec-coverage (leaf, gate) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Model-judged but admissible on the convergence path (ADR-040 §5 / #2040): its
# standard is the issue, produced by intake OUTSIDE this cycle, so the judged
# party cannot re-author it.
spec-coverage:
  gate: auto
  roles: [spec_coverage]
  # A product owner asks "was what was asked for delivered?" — intent-seeking,
  # which is wrong for judging an assertion against a SPEC (the bug there
  # survives charity) and exactly right here, where the question IS about intent.
  persona: product-owner
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── test-author (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not sit on the convergence path.
# Its work is verified mechanically downstream — the test stage runs the
# assertions and acceptance-gate proves they discriminate.
test-author:
  gate: auto
  roles: [test_author]
  # #2188: no authored assertions → the cycle stops before build. Otherwise build
  # writes its own tests, the defect #2022 exists to prevent (#1849 run
  # 35949629759). Its failure is retried first (the stage's `retry:` budget).
  blocking: true
  stage_timeout_s: 900
  router:
    # #2188: the same budget as build — authoring a 15–25 SPEC contract is
    # build-sized work (#1849: two 600s calls both timed out mid-write).
    # #2225: per CALL now — test-author loops until it says it is done, like
    # build, so a big contract takes more calls instead of overrunning one.
    # At most 4 calls: timeouts that are not back-to-back let the loop go on,
    # so the ceiling is calls × timeout — 60 min here (review #2229).
    timeout_s: 900
    max_turns: 0
    max_iterations: 4

# ─── spec-correspondence (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not gate. Its finding reaches
# test-author on the next iteration through the summary channel.
spec-correspondence:
  gate: auto
  roles: [spec_correspondence]
  # #1627: personas were consumed only by review lenses and NO template carried
  # a persona: key, so a persona manifest resolved to nothing. This is the first
  # stage-level binding. QA assures traceability; it does not test — which is
  # what separates it from test-strategist, whose instinct shown a mismatched
  # assertion is to repair it and answer yes.
  persona: quality-assurance
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── assertion-integrity (leaf, gate) ────────────────────────────────────────
# Mechanical, no model.route — so it MAY gate (ADR-040 §5).
assertion-integrity:
  gate: auto
  roles: [assertion_integrity]
  stage_timeout_s: 600

# ─── issue-acceptance (leaf, gate) ───────────────────────────────────────────
# #1849: the finished change against the ISSUE. A model call on the convergence
# path is allowed for the same reason as spec-coverage (ADR-040 §5 as amended by
# #2040): its standard is the issue, which the judged stages cannot re-author.
issue-acceptance:
  gate: auto
  roles: [issue_acceptance]
  # Same question spec-coverage asks of the design — "was what was asked for
  # delivered?" — now asked of the code.
  persona: product-owner
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── build_test_cycle (cycle) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 §2/§5): the cycle re-runs build/test then the decomposed
# mechanical gates (shape-floor, acceptance-gate, secret-scan) and finally the
# gate-aggregator, which collapses every must-pass gate into ONE convergence
# verdict. exit_when fires on gate-aggregator.verdict == pass — the ADR-019
# fail-closed contract re-expressed as a single composable construct (ADR-040 §5).
# (#1129 Change C, ADR-012: the lint/coverage/mutation read-out gates were
# DROPPED as cycle members — they were redundant. mutation and lint both run in
# the test suite (run-tests.sh --tier all / npm test, which the `test` cycle
# member runs), so a lint or mutation regression fails the `test` gate directly.
# coverage is NOT folded into the suite — it stays enforced by the dedicated CI
# `coverage` job (re-running it inside --tier all would trip the #983 re-entrancy
# guard; see ADR-012 "Coverage gating"). The lint-gate/coverage-gate/mutation-gate
# plugins remain canonical (ADR-013) but dormant for future reuse.)
# The individual gates are NON-blocking (no blocking:true):
# they emit verdict-in-artifact (ADR-004) and the cycle iterates-to-fix; the loop
# converges via exit_when, never via per-gate hard-blocks. max_iterations: 3.
# Nested in delivery_loop (#2271): running out of rounds hands back to that loop,
# which goes round from design.
build_test_cycle:
  type: cycle
  description: Build, test, and run the mechanical gates until gate-aggregator passes
  flow:
    # #2022: test-author runs FIRST. It authors the acceptance assertions from
    # the design's SPEC sentences before build implements against them, so the
    # code and the assertion are two independent readings rather than two
    # artifacts of one. It never sees the diff.
    - test-author
    # #2034: judges whether each assertion tests what its SPEC SAYS — the one
    # link execution cannot reach (a passing test proves the implementation
    # satisfies the ASSERTION, never that the assertion satisfies the SENTENCE).
    # Before build, because its question needs the requirement and the assertion
    # and not the implementation — which at this point does not exist yet, so
    # its isolation is a fact of placement rather than a rule to enforce.
    - spec-correspondence
    - build
    - test
    - shape-floor
    - acceptance-gate
    - secret-scan
    # #2022: mechanical backstop. The spawn denies build Edit() on the declared
    # TESTFILES, but #1919 P5 measured that a Write(...) deny rule matches
    # nothing — prevention is incomplete by construction. A fail here makes the
    # aggregate non-pass, so the cycle iterates rather than converging on a
    # rewritten assertion.
    - assertion-integrity
    # #1849: the finished change judged against the ISSUE, not the SPECs — the
    # only check after spec-coverage that reads the issue at all. A convergence
    # gate, so gate-aggregator's roster makes it must-pass; each unmet
    # requirement is a numbered finding.
    - issue-acceptance
    - gate-aggregator
  exit_when:
    stage: gate-aggregator
    field: verdict
    op: eq
    value: pass
  max_iterations: 3
  on_max: continue
  # The cycle CONVERGES rather than spinning build(no-op)→…→gate-aggregator(fail)
  # because the aggregator's consolidated gate-feedback.md reaches build. B2
  # (ADR-040): the gate-aggregator is the SINGLE collector of failure detail,
  # merging every failing mechanical gate into one document. It used to arrive
  # through a feedback: wire plus a bespoke reader; #1979 retired both — the
  # aggregator marks that output `summary: true` (#1976) and the engine injects
  # it, framed by verdict, with no per-consumer wiring.
# ─── intake (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
intake:
  gate: auto
  roles: [intake]
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── plan (leaf) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
plan:
  gate: auto
  roles: [planner]
  stage_timeout_s: 1200
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    # 45 (raised from the 25 default, #1442) — same starvation the impact stage
    # hit (#impact-max-turns): scope exploration needs headroom. The planner is
    # also told this budget in its prompt and biased to converge before it runs out.
    max_turns: 45

# ─── design (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ───────────────────────────────
design:
  gate: auto
  roles: [designer]
  stage_timeout_s: 3900
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 600
    max_turns: 0

# ─── design-gate (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ──────────────────────────
# T0 tool gate (ADR-046, #1218): PRE-build mechanical structural gate. Pure grep
# over design.md (NO LLM, NO baseline — ADR-037 §3). Runs the 5 structural
# checks (scope non-empty; acceptance block well-formed; every SPEC has a status
# — [code], [no-code] or [done] with evidence that exists (ADR-069); every [code]
# SPEC declares a TESTFILE; WIRING present/none + paths exist) and reports ALL
# violations in ONE pass. verdict-in-artifact; the design_verify_cycle exit_when
# reads design-gate.verdict == pass. Bound by role design_gate.
design-gate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [design_gate]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── build (leaf, cycle member) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
build:
  gate: auto
  roles: [builder]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 900
    max_turns: 0

# ─── test (leaf, cycle member) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
test:
  gate: auto
  roles: [tester]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── shape-floor (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1134): un-gameable shape-floor check. verdict-in-artifact.
shape-floor:
  gate: auto
  roles: [shape_floor]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── acceptance-gate (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
# Mechanical (non-LLM) acceptance-contract gate (ADR-036, #922). No-op pass when
# the design acceptance block is absent (its design input is required:false in the
# manifest — design already emits the SPEC/WIRING block). Its gate_result feeds
# the acceptance→build feedback edge above.
# ADR-036 #1188: negctl_timeout_s bounds each SPEC negative-control / reachability
# test run (seconds). A timeout is classified INFRA (non-terminal), never a
# violation. Override per-run with ZBUILD_NEGCTL_TIMEOUT (env wins).
acceptance-gate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [acceptance_gate]
  negctl_timeout_s: 60
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 600
    max_turns: 10

# ─── secret-scan (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1136): blocks hardcoded secrets/.env in the diff.
# verdict-in-artifact (skip on empty diff).
secret-scan:
  gate: auto
  roles: [secret_scan]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── gate-aggregator (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
# T0 convergence aggregator (ADR-040 §2/§5, #1137): collapses the must-pass gate
# set into ONE verdict. This is the cycle's exit_when source and the single
# merge-blocking construct in the decomposed pipeline. verdict-in-artifact.
gate-aggregator:
  gate: auto
  roles: [gate_aggregator]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── review_lenses (map group, ADVISORY) ─────────────────────────────────────
# issue #1295 (ADR-047 §2): converted from `type: parallel` to `type: map`.
# Each element (security, performance, red-team, correctness, scope) becomes one
# work unit dispatched to the review-lens plugin (provides.role: review_lens).
# `as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID` maps each element into the env var the review-lens
# plugin already reads to derive the lens identity — so the plugin is unchanged
# from its per-stage form. This eliminates the five separate lens-* stage
# definitions while preserving the same five isolated LLM calls and the same
# lens-<element>.json artifact names (ADR-038 §2 isolated-call discipline).
#
# aggregate: advisory — this group is NEVER on a merge-blocking path (ADR-040 §4).
# Convergence is owned by the build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator exit_when above;
# the B5 (#1137) no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
review_lenses:
  type: map
  over: lenses
  elements:
    - security
    - performance
    - red-team
    - correctness
    - scope
    - sre
  roles: [review_lens]
  as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID
  max_parallel: 4
  on_member_error: continue
  aggregate: advisory
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    max_turns: 25

# ─── review-aggregator (leaf, ADVISORY) ──────────────────────────────────────
# C2 (#1141, ADR-040 §3/§4): merges the review_lenses members' results — the
# lens_result set the engine hands it (ADR-055 §1.4, #1842) — into ONE advisory
# merge-readiness report (review-report.json + review-report.md). Does NO LLM call
# — it merges lens JSON only. Bound by role review_aggregator to
# plugins/agent/review-aggregator. Requires lens_result: with no lens result the
# engine refuses it, and an empty set reports needs_attention, never "ready"
# (#1753). Never recommends a merge action, never blocks.
# The report.json filename is unchanged, so merge / pr-delivery consume it as before.
review-aggregator:
  gate: auto
  roles: [review_aggregator]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── pr (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool stage (ADR-013): opens the pull request; no LLM call.
pr:
  gate: auto
  roles: [pr]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── release (always-run, ADR-054 §7) ────────────────────────────────────────
# Frees live resources — process groups, locks, handles — and DELETES NOTHING,
# so a failed run keeps every byte of its evidence on disk. The teardown plugin
# pins its own scope to `release`; `purge` is operator-only and unreachable from
# any run path (`zbuild clean --purge`).
#
# timeout_s is 30 and is load-bearing, not a formality: this stage runs inside
# the EXIT trap, so a cleanup hook that blocks would turn Ctrl-C into a hang —
# the exact class of bug the mechanism exists to prevent.
release:
  gate: auto
  roles: [teardown]
  stage_timeout_s: 30
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# ─── persist (always-run, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ───────────────────────────
# Snapshots the artifact area to zbuild/state/issue-<N> and PUSHES it, on every
# exit path. Runs AFTER release, and that order is load-bearing: release frees
# live resources and must stay fast, while this does network I/O and can block
# on auth or a dead remote. Persist last means a bad network can never delay an
# abort.
#
# timeout_s is 120, four times release's 30. A push crosses the network; a
# process-group kill does not.
persist:
  gate: auto
  roles: [persist]
  stage_timeout_s: 120
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# ─── hydrate (first in flow, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ────────────────────────
# Pulls prior artifacts for this issue out of zbuild/state/issue-<N> so each
# stage's prior-output seam can seed from earlier work. Runs BEFORE intake, and
# is NOT always-run — there is nothing to hydrate at the end of a run.
#
# It fetches origin's copy first, which is what makes a fresh CI clone able to
# restore at all; a LOCAL snapshot still wins on read, because it may carry work
# an earlier push never delivered.
hydrate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [hydrate]
  router:
    timeout_s: 60
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

id: simple
name: Simple Pipeline
extends: null

# ADR-037 §4: per-template merge policy. Wired to runtime behavior in #975.
merge_policy: auto_unless_flagged

defaults:
  strategy: map

# ─── Flow ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Simplified pipeline (ADR-037 EPIC #966 / ADR-040 EPIC #1129): 7 top-level flow
# units — intake, plan, design, build_test_cycle, review_lenses, review-aggregator,
# pr — where build_test_cycle groups the build/test leaves plus the decomposed
# mechanical gate stages, and review_lenses is the advisory lens group.
#
# I10-A..C historically wrapped build/test/objective-gate in build_test_cycle.
# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 — amends ADR-013/ADR-021/ADR-019; executes ADR-037 §6) CUT
# OVER convergence from the retired monolithic objective-gate to the composable
# mechanical gates + gate-aggregator; the objective-gate plugin was then removed
# in B7 (#1139). The single merge-blocking construct is the gate-aggregator
# verdict (ADR-040 §5), reached via the cycle's exit_when.
#
# C3 (#1142, ADR-040 §3 — supersedes ADR-038's single-stage fan-out; ADR-039
# parallel group; follows ADR-030 scope governance) CUTS OVER the lens side: the
# monolithic `review` stage (ADR-038's hand-rolled review-report fan-out, now
# UNREFERENCED here) is replaced by `review_lenses` — a `type: map over: lenses`
# `aggregate: advisory` group (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2; was `type: parallel`) —
# one work unit per lens element — followed by
# `review-aggregator`, which merges the per-lens results into ONE advisory
# merge-readiness report. The lens group is ADVISORY: it NEVER feeds the cycle's
# exit_when/convergence (that remains the gate-aggregator, ADR-040 §5) and never
# blocks merge. The B5 no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
flow:
  - hydrate
  - intake
  - plan
  - delivery_loop
  - review_lenses
  - review-aggregator
  - pr

# ─── always_run (#1831) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Stages that run on EVERY exit path — success, non-zero rc, SIGINT, SIGTERM,
# timeout — in the order listed, after the flow has ended.
#
# This replaces a hardcoded dispatch in the runner's EXIT trap, which named one
# plugin by DIRECTORY (`plugins/tool/teardown`) and degraded silently to a no-op
# if it was absent. "Runs on every exit path" is a property of the FLOW, so it
# belongs in the template that defines the flow — not at a line number inside a
# 3000-line runner, where an edit can drop it without anything noticing. #1878
# found exactly that failure in the sibling mechanism: the snapshot was never
# called.
#
# An always-run stage is NOT part of `flow:` and never enters the flow's stage
# list: it has no place in the pipeline's data dependencies and must not affect
# convergence, verdicts, or the run's exit status.
#
# Each entry is an ordinary top-level stage section — resolved by `roles:` like
# any other stage, and bounded by its own `router.timeout_s`. A name here with
# no section, or a section with no `roles:`, REFUSES the template rather than
# quietly running nothing.
always_run:
  - release
  - persist

# ─── delivery_loop (cycle) — #2271, ADR-068 ─────────────────────────────────
# One outer loop holds the design loop and the build loop. Every stage sees
# every finding and says in its own result what it did about each; the engine
# never decides who owns a finding, and nothing jumps backwards.
#   - A design loop that runs out of rounds ends this round (build is skipped)
#     and this loop goes round. When this loop's rounds are spent, the run stops.
delivery_loop:
  type: cycle
  description: Design, then build, until both pass — going round when a finding needs design
  flow:
    - design_verify_cycle
    - build_test_cycle
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: design_verify_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: build_test_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: halt

# ─── design_verify_cycle (cycle) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-046 (#1218, EPIC #1216): give the design stage an independent verifier that
# loops back TO it BEFORE the build cycle — so design/contract defects are caught
# where they are authored, not deep in the build cycle. Modelled on standard.yaml's
# design_impact_cycle (standard.yaml:40-67), which simple.yaml historically lacked.
#
# Members: design → design-gate. design-gate is a T0 tool (ADR-037 §3): a pure-grep
# PRE-build structural gate over design.md + the red-first stubs design writes. It
# is BOTH a cycle member AND convergence:gate, so the typed-aggregator preflight
# rule (A) is satisfied by binding exit_when directly to it — a single gate, no
# separate aggregator needed (contrast build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator, which
# rolls up MANY gates). exit_when fires on design-gate.verdict == pass.
# max_iterations: 2, on_max: halt (#2176): a contract the gate still rejects is
# not built. Nested in delivery_loop (#2271), running out of rounds ends that
# loop's round — build is skipped — and the outer loop goes round.
#
# Feedback: design.design → design.prior_design (self-edge) — mirrors
# design_impact_cycle so iter N+1 refines rather than re-creates (#773 lesson).
#
design_verify_cycle:
  type: cycle
  description: Verify the design contract is build-ready until design-gate passes
  flow:
    - design
    # #1683: does the design cover what the ISSUE asked for? Design is the only
    # reader of the issue, so nothing else confirms the SPECs are a faithful
    # statement of the ask. Inside the cycle, so a finding reaches design itself
    # on the next iteration.
    - spec-coverage
    - design-gate
  # #1284/ADR-047 multi-condition: BOTH must hold. spec-coverage may gate under
  # ADR-040 §5 as amended by #2040 — the standard it judges against is the
  # ISSUE, which design cannot re-author, so the only way to converge is to
  # actually cover it.
  #
  # `ne uncovered` rather than `eq covered`: `unreadable` must not stall the
  # cycle. intake writes a placeholder when the issue fetch fails (#1804), and
  # failing closed there would break every offline run for a condition that is
  # not design's fault. The finding still ships in the summary.
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: design-gate, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: spec-coverage, field: verdict, op: ne, value: uncovered }
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: halt
  feedback:
    - from:
        stage: design
        output: design
      to:
        stage: design
        input: design
        required: false

# ─── spec-coverage (leaf, gate) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Model-judged but admissible on the convergence path (ADR-040 §5 / #2040): its
# standard is the issue, produced by intake OUTSIDE this cycle, so the judged
# party cannot re-author it.
spec-coverage:
  gate: auto
  roles: [spec_coverage]
  # A product owner asks "was what was asked for delivered?" — intent-seeking,
  # which is wrong for judging an assertion against a SPEC (the bug there
  # survives charity) and exactly right here, where the question IS about intent.
  persona: product-owner
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── test-author (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not sit on the convergence path.
# Its work is verified mechanically downstream — the test stage runs the
# assertions and acceptance-gate proves they discriminate.
test-author:
  gate: auto
  roles: [test_author]
  # #2188: no authored assertions → the cycle stops before build. Otherwise build
  # writes its own tests, the defect #2022 exists to prevent (#1849 run
  # 35949629759). Its failure is retried first (the stage's `retry:` budget).
  blocking: true
  stage_timeout_s: 900
  router:
    # #2188: the same budget as build — authoring a 15–25 SPEC contract is
    # build-sized work (#1849: two 600s calls both timed out mid-write).
    # #2225: per CALL now — test-author loops until it says it is done, like
    # build, so a big contract takes more calls instead of overrunning one.
    # At most 4 calls: timeouts that are not back-to-back let the loop go on,
    # so the ceiling is calls × timeout — 60 min here (review #2229).
    timeout_s: 900
    max_turns: 0
    max_iterations: 4

# ─── spec-correspondence (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────
# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not gate. Its finding reaches
# test-author on the next iteration through the summary channel.
spec-correspondence:
  gate: auto
  roles: [spec_correspondence]
  # #1627: personas were consumed only by review lenses and NO template carried
  # a persona: key, so a persona manifest resolved to nothing. This is the first
  # stage-level binding. QA assures traceability; it does not test — which is
  # what separates it from test-strategist, whose instinct shown a mismatched
  # assertion is to repair it and answer yes.
  persona: quality-assurance
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── assertion-integrity (leaf, gate) ────────────────────────────────────────
# Mechanical, no model.route — so it MAY gate (ADR-040 §5).
assertion-integrity:
  gate: auto
  roles: [assertion_integrity]
  stage_timeout_s: 600

# ─── issue-acceptance (leaf, gate) ───────────────────────────────────────────
# #1849: the finished change against the ISSUE. A model call on the convergence
# path is allowed for the same reason as spec-coverage (ADR-040 §5 as amended by
# #2040): its standard is the issue, which the judged stages cannot re-author.
issue-acceptance:
  gate: auto
  roles: [issue_acceptance]
  # Same question spec-coverage asks of the design — "was what was asked for
  # delivered?" — now asked of the code.
  persona: product-owner
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── build_test_cycle (cycle) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 §2/§5): the cycle re-runs build/test then the decomposed
# mechanical gates (shape-floor, acceptance-gate, secret-scan) and finally the
# gate-aggregator, which collapses every must-pass gate into ONE convergence
# verdict. exit_when fires on gate-aggregator.verdict == pass — the ADR-019
# fail-closed contract re-expressed as a single composable construct (ADR-040 §5).
# (#1129 Change C, ADR-012: the lint/coverage/mutation read-out gates were
# DROPPED as cycle members — they were redundant. mutation and lint both run in
# the test suite (run-tests.sh --tier all / npm test, which the `test` cycle
# member runs), so a lint or mutation regression fails the `test` gate directly.
# coverage is NOT folded into the suite — it stays enforced by the dedicated CI
# `coverage` job (re-running it inside --tier all would trip the #983 re-entrancy
# guard; see ADR-012 "Coverage gating"). The lint-gate/coverage-gate/mutation-gate
# plugins remain canonical (ADR-013) but dormant for future reuse.)
# The individual gates are NON-blocking (no blocking:true):
# they emit verdict-in-artifact (ADR-004) and the cycle iterates-to-fix; the loop
# converges via exit_when, never via per-gate hard-blocks. max_iterations: 3.
# Nested in delivery_loop (#2271): running out of rounds hands back to that loop,
# which goes round from design.
build_test_cycle:
  type: cycle
  description: Build, test, and run the mechanical gates until gate-aggregator passes
  flow:
    # #2022: test-author runs FIRST. It authors the acceptance assertions from
    # the design's SPEC sentences before build implements against them, so the
    # code and the assertion are two independent readings rather than two
    # artifacts of one. It never sees the diff.
    - test-author
    # #2034: judges whether each assertion tests what its SPEC SAYS — the one
    # link execution cannot reach (a passing test proves the implementation
    # satisfies the ASSERTION, never that the assertion satisfies the SENTENCE).
    # Before build, because its question needs the requirement and the assertion
    # and not the implementation — which at this point does not exist yet, so
    # its isolation is a fact of placement rather than a rule to enforce.
    - spec-correspondence
    - build
    - test
    - shape-floor
    - acceptance-gate
    - secret-scan
    # #2022: mechanical backstop. The spawn denies build Edit() on the declared
    # TESTFILES, but #1919 P5 measured that a Write(...) deny rule matches
    # nothing — prevention is incomplete by construction. A fail here makes the
    # aggregate non-pass, so the cycle iterates rather than converging on a
    # rewritten assertion.
    - assertion-integrity
    # #1849: the finished change judged against the ISSUE, not the SPECs — the
    # only check after spec-coverage that reads the issue at all. A convergence
    # gate, so gate-aggregator's roster makes it must-pass; each unmet
    # requirement is a numbered finding.
    - issue-acceptance
    - gate-aggregator
  exit_when:
    stage: gate-aggregator
    field: verdict
    op: eq
    value: pass
  max_iterations: 3
  on_max: continue
  # The cycle CONVERGES rather than spinning build(no-op)→…→gate-aggregator(fail)
  # because the aggregator's consolidated gate-feedback.md reaches build. B2
  # (ADR-040): the gate-aggregator is the SINGLE collector of failure detail,
  # merging every failing mechanical gate into one document. It used to arrive
  # through a feedback: wire plus a bespoke reader; #1979 retired both — the
  # aggregator marks that output `summary: true` (#1976) and the engine injects
  # it, framed by verdict, with no per-consumer wiring.
# ─── intake (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
intake:
  gate: auto
  roles: [intake]
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── plan (leaf) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
plan:
  gate: auto
  roles: [planner]
  stage_timeout_s: 1200
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    # 45 (raised from the 25 default, #1442) — same starvation the impact stage
    # hit (#impact-max-turns): scope exploration needs headroom. The planner is
    # also told this budget in its prompt and biased to converge before it runs out.
    max_turns: 45

# ─── design (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ───────────────────────────────
design:
  gate: auto
  roles: [designer]
  stage_timeout_s: 3900
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 600
    max_turns: 0

# ─── design-gate (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ──────────────────────────
# T0 tool gate (ADR-046, #1218): PRE-build mechanical structural gate. Pure grep
# over design.md (NO LLM, NO baseline — ADR-037 §3). Runs the 5 structural
# checks (scope non-empty; acceptance block well-formed; every SPEC has a status
# — [code], [no-code] or [done] with evidence that exists (ADR-069); every [code]
# SPEC declares a TESTFILE; WIRING present/none + paths exist) and reports ALL
# violations in ONE pass. verdict-in-artifact; the design_verify_cycle exit_when
# reads design-gate.verdict == pass. Bound by role design_gate.
design-gate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [design_gate]
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── build (leaf, cycle member) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
build:
  gate: auto
  roles: [builder]
  stage_timeout_s: 4200
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 900
    max_turns: 0

# ─── test (leaf, cycle member) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
test:
  gate: auto
  roles: [tester]
  stage_timeout_s: 5400
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── shape-floor (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1134): un-gameable shape-floor check. verdict-in-artifact.
shape-floor:
  gate: auto
  roles: [shape_floor]
  stage_timeout_s: 600
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── acceptance-gate (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
# Mechanical (non-LLM) acceptance-contract gate (ADR-036, #922). No-op pass when
# the design acceptance block is absent (its design input is required:false in the
# manifest — design already emits the SPEC/WIRING block). Its gate_result feeds
# the acceptance→build feedback edge above.
# ADR-036 #1188: negctl_timeout_s bounds each SPEC negative-control / reachability
# test run (seconds). A timeout is classified INFRA (non-terminal), never a
# violation. Override per-run with ZBUILD_NEGCTL_TIMEOUT (env wins).
acceptance-gate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [acceptance_gate]
  negctl_timeout_s: 60
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 600
    max_turns: 10

# ─── secret-scan (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1136): blocks hardcoded secrets/.env in the diff.
# verdict-in-artifact (skip on empty diff).
secret-scan:
  gate: auto
  roles: [secret_scan]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── gate-aggregator (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
# T0 convergence aggregator (ADR-040 §2/§5, #1137): collapses the must-pass gate
# set into ONE verdict. This is the cycle's exit_when source and the single
# merge-blocking construct in the decomposed pipeline. verdict-in-artifact.
gate-aggregator:
  gate: auto
  roles: [gate_aggregator]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── review_lenses (map group, ADVISORY) ─────────────────────────────────────
# issue #1295 (ADR-047 §2): converted from `type: parallel` to `type: map`.
# Each element (security, performance, red-team, correctness, scope) becomes one
# work unit dispatched to the review-lens plugin (provides.role: review_lens).
# `as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID` maps each element into the env var the review-lens
# plugin already reads to derive the lens identity — so the plugin is unchanged
# from its per-stage form. This eliminates the five separate lens-* stage
# definitions while preserving the same five isolated LLM calls and the same
# lens-<element>.json artifact names (ADR-038 §2 isolated-call discipline).
#
# aggregate: advisory — this group is NEVER on a merge-blocking path (ADR-040 §4).
# Convergence is owned by the build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator exit_when above;
# the B5 (#1137) no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
review_lenses:
  type: map
  over: lenses
  elements:
    - security
    - performance
    - red-team
    - correctness
    - scope
    - sre
  roles: [review_lens]
  as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID
  max_parallel: 4
  on_member_error: continue
  aggregate: advisory
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    max_turns: 25

# ─── review-aggregator (leaf, ADVISORY) ──────────────────────────────────────
# C2 (#1141, ADR-040 §3/§4): merges the review_lenses members' results — the
# lens_result set the engine hands it (ADR-055 §1.4, #1842) — into ONE advisory
# merge-readiness report (review-report.json + review-report.md). Does NO LLM call
# — it merges lens JSON only. Bound by role review_aggregator to
# plugins/agent/review-aggregator. Requires lens_result: with no lens result the
# engine refuses it, and an empty set reports needs_attention, never "ready"
# (#1753). Never recommends a merge action, never blocks.
# The report.json filename is unchanged, so merge / pr-delivery consume it as before.
review-aggregator:
  gate: auto
  roles: [review_aggregator]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── pr (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool stage (ADR-013): opens the pull request; no LLM call.
pr:
  gate: auto
  roles: [pr]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── release (always-run, ADR-054 §7) ────────────────────────────────────────
# Frees live resources — process groups, locks, handles — and DELETES NOTHING,
# so a failed run keeps every byte of its evidence on disk. The teardown plugin
# pins its own scope to `release`; `purge` is operator-only and unreachable from
# any run path (`zbuild clean --purge`).
#
# timeout_s is 30 and is load-bearing, not a formality: this stage runs inside
# the EXIT trap, so a cleanup hook that blocks would turn Ctrl-C into a hang —
# the exact class of bug the mechanism exists to prevent.
release:
  gate: auto
  roles: [teardown]
  stage_timeout_s: 30
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# ─── persist (always-run, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ───────────────────────────
# Snapshots the artifact area to zbuild/state/issue-<N> and PUSHES it, on every
# exit path. Runs AFTER release, and that order is load-bearing: release frees
# live resources and must stay fast, while this does network I/O and can block
# on auth or a dead remote. Persist last means a bad network can never delay an
# abort.
#
# timeout_s is 120, four times release's 30. A push crosses the network; a
# process-group kill does not.
persist:
  gate: auto
  roles: [persist]
  stage_timeout_s: 120
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# ─── hydrate (first in flow, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ────────────────────────
# Pulls prior artifacts for this issue out of zbuild/state/issue-<N> so each
# stage's prior-output seam can seed from earlier work. Runs BEFORE intake, and
# is NOT always-run — there is nothing to hydrate at the end of a run.
#
# It fetches origin's copy first, which is what makes a fresh CI clone able to
# restore at all; a LOCAL snapshot still wins on read, because it may carry work
# an earlier push never delivered.
hydrate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [hydrate]
  router:
    timeout_s: 60
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50
